News.title: Brit uni student tortured to death in ‘cemetery of the living’ after being mistaken for spy – as three convicted
News.content:
Next

THREE Egyptian state agents have been convicted of the kidnapping of a Cambridge University student who was killed in a prison known as “the cemetery of the living”.

Giulio Regeni was found beside the Cairo-Alexandria highway in 2016, with his body transfigured by severe torture, including cigarette burns, broken teeth, and fractured bones.



An autopsy carried out in Rome confirmed that the 28-year-old had been beaten, burnt, stabbed and probably flogged on the soles of his feet over a period of four days.

Every one of his toes and fingers was shattered. He died when his neck was snapped.



A decade later, an Italian court has sentenced Maj. Magdi Ibrahim Abdelal Sharif, Col. Uhsam Helmi and Athar Kamel Mohamed Ibrahim for his kidnapping.

A fourth defendant, Gen. Tariq Sabir, was acquitted of murder.



The ruling marks the most significant judicial milestone yet in the quest for justice.

Rome’s chief prosecutor Francesco Lo Voi welcomed the outcome, saying it was achieved despite no “meaningful cooperation” from Egypt.



All defendants were tried in absentia.

“We are satisfied for having brought the case out of the quagmire into which it had risked sinking,” Lo Voi told reporters after the verdict.

A lawyer for Regeni’s family, Alessandra Ballerini, said the sentence meant that “all citizens of the world can feel safer.”



In a statement, she added that the sentence would force authoritarian regimes “to remember that people’s dignity is inviolable.”

The case surrounding his death became a diplomatic crisis and strained relations between Italy and Egypt.

Egyptian authorities repeatedly denied state involvement and disputed the findings of the Italian investigation.

The investigation was marked by years of tortuous disputes over evidence and judicial cooperation.

Italian magistrates accused Egyptian authorities of withholding key information requested through international legal channels.



Regeni, a PhD student at Cambridge, had travelled to Egypt to carry out research on local trade unions and workers’ conditions.

Alarm bells were first raised when he published anti-government findings in an Italian left-wing newspaper.

Earlier this year, prosecutor Sergio Colaiocco said at the trial that Egyptian officials were “erroneously convinced that he was an English spy” due to his movements, connections and work.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Regeni first went missing on January 25, 2016, with his remains found nine days later.

He was last seen leaving his Cairo flat as he went out to meet a friend in the city before reportedly disappearing at the Izbakiya police station in a white van.

News.title: If you REALLY care about cost of living, PM, start with fuel duty. So what IS his plan?
News.content:
POLITICS FIX If you REALLY care about cost of living, PM, start with fuel duty. So what IS his plan?







Next

ANDY Burnham has pledged to lead a “cost of living government” but is finding himself at the mercy of global shocks.

The war in Iran has pushed up the price of oil and now a litre diesel is on the cusp of hitting £2.



Millions of drivers being clobbered at the pumps are looking at their PM to intervene and give them the “breathing space” he has long promised.

So does Andy have a plan?



The most obvious thing he could do is give people relief on fuel duty, which pushes up the cost of filling up.

Fuel duty is set to rise in January when Labour ditches the current 5p cut, and could then increase yet again in March if ministers fail to keep a 15-year freeze.



Chancellor John Healey hinted yesterday he could step in to stop the impending rise in fuel costs.

He said: “So look, I’m concerned, I’m conscious of the pressure this is putting on people, on businesses as well as people at the pumps, and this is a government that will do what we can to give people a bit of breathing space.”

But both Burnham and Healey are finding that cash is in short supply in this government and they lack the money to fund their ambitious plans.

The PM will today tell the public he wants to have an “honest conversation” about ways he can tackle pressing issues like social care and defence.



It has fuelled speculation he could either axe the pensions triple lock, or embark on big tax rises to make the sums add up.

Yet while such policies might get a cheer at the Labour conference in Liverpool, squeezing Brits for more of their money might be a flop with voters.

News.title: Two morgue workers at Lucy Letby’s former hospital win £30k over lack of PPE to protect them from dead bodies
News.content:
Next

TWO morgue workers at killer Lucy Letby’s former hospital have won almost £30,000 after complaining they lacked PPE to protect them from splashback from dead bodies.

Porters John Crayton and Thomas Jones raised concerns about hygiene and psychological harm caused by uncovered corpses at the Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust.



Mr Crayton and Mr Jones both worked as porters at Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust in Chester, Cheshire.

They would take deceased patients who had passed away either in the hospital or in the community to the hospital’s mortuary.



In the same role at a previous hospital, Mr Crayton had always transported bodies when they were already in body bags and they were not responsible for transporting deceased people from the community to the refrigerators.

He said that while working at the Chester hospital, he had got ‘splashback from fluid with no protection for the forearms due to the [hospital’s] bare to elbow policy’ and inadequate PPE.



In violation of the hospital’s anonymous complaints policy, a manager found out about Crayton’s grievance and revoked his mortuary access.

The manager claimed it was because he was suspicious that their complaints about DNA transference on the uncovered bodies meant they had ‘something to hide’.

He and Jones went off sick afterwards, leading to colleagues speculating he had done “something inappropriate”.

The two men took the hospital, where Letby murdered seven babies, to an employment tribunal in Manchester.



The hospital has been ordered to pay Mr Crayton £2,121 net in compensation for wage loss and £15,000 in compensation for injury to feelings.

It must also pay Mr Jones £1,439 net in compensation for wage loss and £11,000 in compensation for injury to feelings.

News.title: John Healey must use Budget to turn words into bold action and confront welfare spending head-on
News.content:
Welfare’s state







Next

ANDY Burnham has perfected the politics of optimism — but charisma can’t fill the black hole in the nation’s finances.

After ten weeks in power, it’s becoming increasingly clear that he’s leading a government that is high on hope but dangerously low on funds.



John Healey practically admitted it yesterday in his first Labour conference speech as Chancellor.

He gave activists a blunt reality check, warning there is “simply no cash left” to fund their grand dream of fantasy giveaways in the Budget next month.



The problem is, Labour is addicted to giving away cash through the benefits system.

Healey delivered some home truths about welfare spending, saying it was “not progressive” to allow the benefits bill to continue to balloon and he had a “moral duty” to get claimants into work.



But will he have the stomach to face down Labour’s bleeding-heart MPs?

His biggest stumbling block will be backbench rebels who last year derailed a paltry £5billion cut to the £334billion welfare bill planned by Sir Keir Starmer.

They will be emboldened by new figures showing that one in five people living in Labour constituencies claims Universal Credit or PIP.

The average Labour MP has 22,600 benefit claimants as potential voters.



More taxpayer-funded back-to-work schemes masquerading as benefit reforms will take years to make an impact — and handouts will keep on rising before they do.

The Chancellor must use his Budget to turn his words into bold action — and confront welfare spending head-on.

It’s his — and Britain’s — only hope.

Border farce

ANGELA Rayner has teamed up with the same deluded left-wing Labour MPs to blow a hole in the Government’s plans to tackle mass migration.

The newly returned Cabinet firebrand led the charge against tougher settlement rules for foreign arrivals.



And her explosive weekend outburst — a wild breach of Cabinet discipline — appears to have panicked the Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood into watering down her proposals.

It’s yet more proof that when it comes to getting a grip on our borders, Labour doesn’t have a clue.

Don’t be a fuel

MOTORISTS are reeling at the pumps as diesel rockets to around £2 a litre.

With the price of filling a family car soaring past £110, it would be political suicide for the Chancellor to scrap the 5p fuel duty discount in the Budget.

It would hit not only working commuters but also millions of white-van tradesmen and women fighting to keep their businesses on the road.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

John Healey has made positive noises about giving drivers “breathing space”.

He should now get on with it and agree to keep it down.

News.title: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is living in an appropriate setting, cops say after wellbeing concerns & ‘King tried to contact him’
News.content:
EXPLORER RIDDLE Sir Ranulph Fiennes is living in an appropriate setting, cops say after wellbeing concerns & ‘King tried to contact him’







Next

SIR Ranulph Fiennes is living in an “appropriate setting” and receiving “suitable care”, cops say.

It comes after concerns were raised about his well-being, prompting the King to try and reach out to the explorer, but to no avail.



Detective Chief Superintendent Claire Jesson, of Cheshire Police, said the force were aware of friends and relatives’ fears over the 82-year-old’s health.

However, they added that there were “no immediate safeguarding concerns” regarding his care.



Ms Jesson said: “Any new information received will be assessed and considered through the appropriate multi-agency arrangements.

“As this is a matter involving an individual’s care and welfare, it would not be appropriate to comment further on personal circumstances.”

The adventurer – who has been out of the public eye for more than two years – has allegedly been given a fake name by his second wife, Louise Millington.

He is thought to have been moved between various care homes, with his whereabouts still unclear to friends and family.



A care home owner in Wales, where the adventurer was reportedly staying for seven weeks earlier this year, told The Telegraph they feared for Ranulph’s health.

They claimed he was being “deprived of his liberty unlawfully” and had contacted a care watchdog with their concerns.

In an extraordinary plea, Louise’s estranged son, Alex Millington-Cotes, said this week: “I believe my mother exerted a controlling influence from the very start of their marriage.”

He said he had had “no luck” persuading two police forces to investigate his step-dad’s whereabouts, after it emerged that King Charles himself had also been blocked from checking in on him last year.

The King was first alerted to Ranulph’s deteriorating condition back in February 2025, when the explorer’s long-standing friend Anton Bowring wrote to him stating he was “in a very poor state”.



According to Anton, the King said he was “most concerned” and wanted to write to Sir Ranulph, his wife Louise and their daughter Elizabeth.

He asked Anton for Louise’s phone number so the Palace could get in touch.

Anton passed on the details, but was later sent a message from Louise saying she was going to change her number because of him.



She warned him she would contact a solicitor and police if he continued, claiming he was causing her husband “immense distress”.

Anton said he had simply thought Sir Ranulph would be “thrilled” to know the King cared about him.

Sir Ranulph, 82, has not been seen in public since giving a video tribute to his late first wife Ginny in October 2024.

Louise, 59, was granted lasting power of attorney over him in November 2024.

Alex, Louise’s estranged son, has launched a fundraising campaign to help challenge the extent of her power of attorney.



He is seeking to raise £55,000 to fund legal action if necessary, with £21,000 raised already.

“I want to ensure his complete free will, the ability to walk outside, see whoever he wants,” he said.

He previously said: “I want to ensure his complete free will, the ability to walk outside, see whoever he wants.”

Friends and family have also raised concerns after being unable to establish where Sir Ranulph is living or even speak to him.

Bear Grylls said: “We have been desperately trying to connect with Ran for a year now, to no avail.”



He added that reports of the explorer’s isolation from loved ones and treatment in care homes were “deeply disturbing”.

Ben Fogle, Joanna Lumley and John Simpson are among other well-known friends to have backed calls for an investigation by the Office of the Public Guardian.

It has been claimed that friends were initially allowed to visit Sir Ranulph if they signed non-disclosure agreements.

But they have reportedly not been told where he is since the start of this year.

The concerns were also raised with the Office of the Public Guardian last year.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Louise has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Man, 20, dies after ‘getting into difficulty’ in lake at UK beauty spot – as his heartbroken family pay tribute
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

LAKE TRAGEDY Man, 20, dies after ‘getting into difficulty’ in lake at UK beauty spot – as his heartbroken family pay tribute







Next

A MAN has died after getting into difficulty in a lake at a UK beauty spot with his heartbroken family now paying tribute.

Mahammed Maim Islan, 20, was reported missing at Llyn Glaslyn in Eryri, also known as Snowdonia, shortly before 7pm on Saturday.

Emergency crews scrambled to the lake alongside Llanberis Mountain Rescue Team after the Londoner vanished in the water.

A desperate search was launched but Mahammed could not be found before the operation was halted overnight.





Rescuers returned to the rugged beauty spot on Sunday morning as specialist police divers joined the hunt.

Shortly before midday, Mahammed’s body was tragically found and recovered from the lake.

His devastated family have now paid tribute to following his death.

They said: “Mahammed was a bright and remarkable young man with a promising future ahead of him.



“He was a devoted son, a loving brother, and a cherished friend whose kindness and character touched the lives of all who knew him.

“His untimely passing has left his family, friends, and wider community heartbroken.

“He will be remembered for the joy he brought to others, the memories he created, and the positive impact he had on those fortunate enough to cross his path.”

They added: “Mahammed will be deeply missed and lovingly remembered by everyone who knew him.



“Our thoughts and sincere condolences remain with his family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.”

The family also thanked the emergency crews and volunteers involved in the search and recovery operation.

Chief Inspector Steve Pawson from North Wales Police said: “Our thoughts remain with the man’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.

“The Coroner has been informed and enquiries are now underway.

“I would like to express my thanks to all emergency responders and mountain rescue volunteers who responded to this incident.”



The coroner has been informed as police continue inquiries into the tragedy.

News.title: New trains could be publicly owned under controversial scheme that could ‘add billions to national debt’
News.content:
RAIL SPLURGE New trains could be publicly owned under controversial scheme that could ‘add billions to national debt’







Next

NEW trains could be publicly owned under a controversial scheme outlined by Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander.

She revealed Labour’s state-owned Great British Railways would take a case-by-case approach to buying rolling stock for the network.



It will decide if private investment, leasing or public ownership would give taxpayers the best value.

But the Tories warned it would add billions to the national debt, just as borrowing costs reach a 30-year high.



Shadow Transport Secretary Richard Holden said the proposals showed Labour were still “in hock to their union pay-masters”.

He added: “Labour are pushing their ideological agenda over getting the trains to run on time, at prices people can afford, and reducing the cost to taxpayers.

“This plan would leave taxpayers on the hook for tens of billions of debt and interest for decades, yet Labour still cannot say what the true cost will be.”

For almost three decades, most passenger trains have been privately owned and leased to operators.

Ms Alexander said: “We will explore whether the state can directly own the new trains we order, helping to ensure our railway delivers the best possible value for passengers.

“Labour is committed to bringing the essentials in life back under stronger public control, opening up opportunities for people across the country and supporting economic growth in every postcode.”



It comes after the Government set a date for the nationalisation of Avanti West Coast services for March next year.

News.title: Putin calls up thousands more soldiers to military despite claiming he ‘not preparing’ for war against Europe
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin has ordered thousands more troops into his military machine just days after insisting Russia is not preparing for war with Europe.

Putin’s sprawling armed forces are now authorised to contain a staggering 2,441,630 personnel – including 1,550,500 active-duty military personnel.



It is the fourth time this year Putin has ordered an expansion of his enormous military establishment, following previous decrees in March, June and late July.

But the latest build-up comes just days after the Russian leader flatly denied he was preparing to plunge Moscow into a wider conflict with Europe.



Putin said: “I want to emphasize once again that we are not preparing for any military action against Europe.

“We have no such plans, and, most importantly, there are no grounds for them.



“There are no real incentives whatsoever to escalate the situation with Europe.”

He accused European countries of deliberately escalating tensions by warning their populations to prepare for a possible Russian attack.

Putin also claimed the rights of Russian speakers were being violated in the Baltic states but insisted Moscow would respond through humanitarian measures and international law.

The Kremlin’s latest military expansion comes barely a week after a parliamentary election Putin had himself portrayed as a test of support for his war.



Putin’s United Russia party tightened its iron grip on the State Duma with a record 355 of its 450 seats, according to near-complete official results.

The vote was the first parliamentary election since the tyrant unleashed his full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

It was held inside Russia and in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine, where the votes are not recognised as legitimate by Kyiv or Western governments.



Putin had urged Russians to use their ballots to demonstrate that “millions of people” stood behind the country’s fighters.

But critics accused the Kremlin of crushing meaningful opposition ahead of the ballot.

And the election was overshadowed by ominous warnings that Putin could use the result to demand even greater sacrifices for his bloody war machine.

The Institute for the Study of War said before the vote that the Kremlin was seeking to present the election as evidence of popular support for Putin’s war.

It warned that could help Moscow justify “long-term societal sacrifices such as mobilization”.



Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has since warned that Russia is already embarking on an additional mobilisation drive.

He said: “In effect, the Russians have already begun mobilisation. They are increasing the number of people they recruit through various means.

“They also plan to increase the recruitment of foreigners, and it is important that the governments of the countries from which Russia recruits people into its ranks counter this.



“We will inform every relevant government.”

Zelensky previously claimed Putin could seek another 300,000 troops following the parliamentary elections – despite repeated Kremlin denials that another mobilisation is being prepared.

And it is not just manpower Putin is pouring into his vast war machine.

Russia is preparing to splurge a record 17.1 trillion roubles – around £153billion – on defence in 2027, according to government documents seen by Reuters.

The eye-watering war chest is around 27 per cent higher than the 13.5 trillion roubles originally budgeted and would be Moscow’s biggest defence spend since Putin unleashed his full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.



A staggering 50 trillion roubles is now set to be pumped into defence over the next three years as the Kremlin bankrolls its mammoth military machine.

And Putin appears prepared to heap further pressure on Russia’s strained finances to pay for it.

Moscow has doubled its estimate for this year’s budget deficit from 1.6 per cent to 3.2 per cent of GDP and increased its net borrowing plan by 26 per cent to five trillion roubles.

Putin’s latest military expansion will now fuel fresh scrutiny of his denials as European countries simultaneously brace themselves against an increasingly menacing Russian threat.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has warned that Moscow could launch “hybrid” attacks against countries backing Ukraine – including Poland.



“These potential strikes would be quote-unquote ‘accidental’ in nature,” he told parliament, citing intelligence.

“[They will be] intended to paralyse or at least weaken the resolve of Nato states to invoke the relevant Nato provisions in the event of aggression against a member country.”

The chilling scenario would see Moscow pile pressure on NATO while sowing uncertainty over whether an incident amounted to a deliberate Russian attack.

And even some of Europe’s biggest holiday hotspots have now been dragged into the terrifying security fears surrounding Putin’s next move.

US intelligence services have reportedly warned European countries of a possible Russian operation involving drones launched from commercial vessels in the Mediterranean.



Spain, France and Italy were named as possible targets in intelligence described by Spanish newspaper El Mundo, according to subsequent reports.

The suspected plot could involve Gerbera-type drones hidden aboard ships before being unleashed from international waters towards southern Europe.

The CIA itself has not publicly released the reported assessment, meaning the alarming scenario remains based on reports of intelligence shared with European governments rather than a publicly confirmed Russian attack plan.

But experts have warned that an assault on civilian areas could create carnage while forcing NATO into a nightmare decision over how to respond.

Intelligence analyst Ryan McBeth told The Sun: “Putin would want to attack these holiday hotspots because you could consider it a soft target.



“If you try to attack military installations, there might be some drone defence but by attacking these holiday hotspots, you’re going to create a mass casualty event.

“Something like that could let countries in Nato know that Putin is serious.

“Putin will understand that most Nato countries would walk away from funding Ukraine rather than get their populations involved in a war.”

He added: “It’s almost like him saying ‘I just killed 20 of your citizens. Now you have a choice’.”

Russian military expert Keir Giles also told The Sun that any such attack could ultimately leave little doubt over who was responsible.



He said: “It might sow confusion temporarily among the victim countries, but eventually there’d be no doubt that this was an overt attack by Moscow.

“And the fact that this may have been under consideration is an indication that Russia may be pushing the boundaries and deciding that it might be time to consider some kind of overt strike.”

Any deliberate Russian armed attack against a NATO member would raise the explosive question of Article 5 – the alliance’s collective-defence commitment.

That could transform Putin’s grinding war against Ukraine into a vastly more dangerous confrontation involving NATO.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The warnings come as Moscow has been accused of increasingly testing Europe with drone incursions, sabotage, cyber operations and other “hybrid” attacks.



Putin has repeatedly denied Russia intends to attack NATO saying “there is no real motive” to escalate the situation with Europe.

News.title: Angela Rayner says meeting rough sleepers 'reminds you what matters' after visit with Andy Burnham
News.content:
Angela Rayner says meeting rough sleepers 'reminds you what matters' after visit with Andy Burnham

EXCLUSIVE: Angela Rayner said meeting rough sleepers 'reminds you of what matters' as she joined Andy Burnham and John Healey on a visit to a homelessness charity

View 4 Images Andy Burnham, Angela Rayner and John Healey visited a homelessness charity on Monday (Image: Andrew Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Angela Rayner said meeting rough sleepers “reminds you of what matters” as she joined Andy Burnham and John Healey on a visit to a homelessness charity on Monday.

‌



The top Cabinet ministers took time out from Labour’s conference to meet people who will be directly affected by their policy to end rough sleeping.

‌



The Prime Minister laughed and chatted with people who had benefited from a homelessness support services in Bootle, just down the road from the conference centre.

‌



Chancellor Mr Healey, who finished his keynote conference speech just an hour before, helped make an apple crumble in the centre’s kitchen, where people learn how to cook and share meals together. Mr Burnham also mucked in by painting a plant box in the sunny, blooming garden, which is tended to by service users at the Independence Initiative.

Ms Rayner, the Housing Secretary, told The Mirror: “I get a lot out of this as well because it reminds you of what matters. Sometimes when you're in Westminster, you talk about stats, you're talking about high-level strategic issues and laws, but it's about how it affects people on the ground and changes people's lives.

Chancellor John Healey urged to end housing benefit freeze hitting low-income families at Budget READ MORE :

View 4 Images The PM painted a plant box during the visit (Image: Andrew Stenning/Daily Mirror)

‌



"This literally changes people's lives. And there's so many volunteers and workers, and I talk about the carers, talk about the workers here that are doing the outreach work, and it really does change people's lives. Like even the smallest thing, that little connection.”

On the day Mr Burnham entered Downing Street in July, the new PM made ending rough sleeping his “first instruction” to officials.

The PM has pledged to offer a place to stay to every rough sleeper by Christmas, with emergency accommodation and help to be rolled out in England later this year. It is backed by increased funding of £442million. He will convene a "first of its kind" national summit on ending rough sleeping this autumn.

‌



Ms Rayner - who chatted with staff and service users at the centre - said: "Speaking to the volunteers and the guys here they said: 'We feel seen for the first time, we feel seen.'

"And then looking at what this place does, it's not just about taking people off the streets. It's about creating a network of support. It's about the wraparound support that people need. Sometimes it's even getting your credit checks, getting your bills sorted out, getting your hospital appointments if you need that, your GP registration."

View 4 Images Andy Burnham helps stack shelves in the pantry at the Independence Initiative (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

‌



Ms Rayner said she is working with mayors and local authorities to increase coordination between services to meet the Christmas deadline to offer a place to every rough sleeper.

She added: "On Friday, I was in my patch in Tameside talking to the police, the council, the homelessness service through the supported living, and really trying to make sure that we're coordinated so that we identify where the problems are and we give people those opportunities.

"So we do it all year round, but there's going to be a huge focus on it this time round to really make sure that the coordination between those services are there, so we can help people, and that's my message to people. This is what we want to do: This whole community effort to help people and get them on the right path."

‌



In her speech to Labour conference on Tuesday, the Housing Secretary will announce changes in the law to maximise councils’ abilities to buy up social rented homes that are being sold by private registered providers.

She will also outline new powers to require public services to work together to prevent homelessness, and ensure homeless households are referred to housing associations and other providers to be housed. The changes will be legislated for as amendments to the Social Housing Bill.

Asked how she will feel if the Government fails in its target to end rough sleeping, Ms Rayner added: "I think government has to change and give people hope."

‌



View 4 Images The Prime Minister laughed and chatted with people at a homelessness support services in Bootle (Image: Andrew Stenning/Daily Mirror)

John Bird, the Big Issue founder, said a whole society approach is needed to eradicate homelessness, which he said must sit alongside a pledge to wipe out poverty.

He told The Mirror: “An ex-rough sleeper and as an ex-you know-homeless guy, I can honestly say that it's getting worse again. When I was a young man and when I was a boy, sleeping rough, running away from home and the police, and all sorts of stuff like that, there was very, very few young people involved in it.

‌



"Now there's an enormous amount of young people, and you see young people who get involved in drugs and they get involved in other things."

Lord Bird said the Government must bring together the public alongside charities, churches, and other organisations to build an alliance to tackle the issue. "It has to be this kind of assembly, this confederation of effort," he said.

"I've been advocating for the creation of a government body, which I hope would be a ministry - the Ministry of Poverty Prevention and Cure - because the problem is nearly all the big money is going in the emergency, and if you spend all your money on the emergency, you don't have any left for prevention or for cure.

‌



"And what I want, Andy Burnham, and I'm going to be a pain in the rear about this one. I will always be reminding him that if you want to eradicate homelessness, you have to begin to eradicate poverty."

Paulene Connell, deputy chief executive of the Independence Initiative, welcomed Mr Burnham's focus on homelessness and rough sleeping, which is often an "invisible" issue to many.

She told The Mirror: "The service users feel invisible and hidden. As staff at times working in a small charity, we're fighting their corner and we feel invisible, so I really welcomed he put it on the agenda. I felt really seen, and so did our service users. They felt we had a voice."

‌



Ms Connell urged the PM to tackle a lack of coordination between public services. She said: "When you actually advocate for somebody, you're in a silo, and you actually have to fight really hard to get that person sort of joined up into the services. Somebody will do a referral, and they perhaps don't chase it.

"In the wider sort of partners, it can be, you know, trying to get somebody mental health assessed if they've got a drug problem. It's not happening. 'Go away and come back in 12 months.' That doesn't work. That makes it worse."

Jim Brett, the chief executive at the initiative, added: "Every human being is so small an angle away from it happening to them as well. We all know that it could easily happen to you, and wouldn't you want that support if it happened to you? We need to be a bit more human about it and actually help people."

‌



It comes as startling new figures show half of people rough sleeping in England have spent time in prison. Former inmates are 40 times more likely to experience rough sleeping than those who have not. The data shows that on a single night in October 2025, there were 4,793 rough sleepers in England, with 49% of those saying they had been in prison in the past.

Campaign group Nacro has warned the government’s drive to end rough sleeping will be scuppered if it does not act.

'I sofa surfed while battling addiction - I'm glad Burnham is taking issue seriously'

A 58-year-old man who sofa surfed while battling addiction has praised Andy Burnham for taking homelessness seriously.

‌



Joey Cullen, who is from Dublin and now lives in Liverpool, met the PM, Angela Rayner and John Healey, at the Independence Initiative on Monday. Joey, who now volunteers at the centre, said the support he received from the initiative gave him a new "start".

"I was kind of sleeping on my mate's sofa. My mum passed away, you know, just before I came over, so I was kind of getting a little bit deeper and deeper into stuff that I shouldn't be doing. So this is where I went for a new start. So I came up to Liverpool and I'm here 11 months now and, yeah, I love it."

Joey said you don't believe everything politicians say on the TV but praised Mr Burnham for taking an interest in how the services work.

Article continues below

He said: "When you've heard so many politicians say so much about so much when they get into power, when you see the people who came here today - the Chancellor, the Lady, and the Prime Minister - and actually taking an interest in what's going on here, that's massive.

"We didn't know until 15 minutes before the man came that he was coming. None of us knew. And, you don't believe everything you see on the TV now, (but) I'm just going to say that he's a gentleman. You know that he put me at ease. I was able to chat to him... he seems really interested in what they're doing."

News.title: Thatcham fire - live: Explosions as huge blaze erupts at industrial estate with trains cancelled
News.content:
The scene in Thatcham following a fire at an industrial park

Residents have reported hearing loud bangs in the area surrounding the Colthrop Business Park near Thatcham in West Berkshire, with GWR trains affected

A huge fire has erupted at an industrial park, with explosions heard from several miles away as local train services grind to a halt.

Loud bangs have been reported by people in the area surrounding the Colthrop Business Park near Thatcham in West Berkshire after the blaze started around 8pm today with massive flames visible next to a railway line.

Multiple fire engines are currently at the scene, with video footage showing huge plumes of smoke billowing across the area.

Great Western Railway has cancelled services between Newbury and Reading. The operator said: "Due to a very large fire near the railway, the room that controls the signals in the Newbury area has been evacuated."

News.title: Wes Streeting asked to probe claims civil servants 'torpedoed' compensation for nuclear test vets
News.content:
Wes Streeting asked to probe claims civil servants 'torpedoed' compensation for nuclear test vets

EXCLUSIVE: Labour peer Kevan Jones has claimed that he has learned alleged briefings from civil servants that 'lawyers were only interested in their fees' were in fact false

View 3 Images Wes Streeting has been asked to look into claims civil servants 'torpedoed' compensation of veterans of the UK's nuclear weapons programme (Image: Jack Taylor/Pool Reuters via AP)

Wes Streeting has been asked to investigate claims civil servants “torpedoed” the government’s compensation deal for veterans of Britain’s nuclear weapons programme.

‌



Labour peer Kevan Jones – a former Veterans Minister and now titled Lord Beamish – has learned his 2009 offer of a £20million payout was never received by lawyers. He said: “I was told they had rejected it out of hand. Civil servants briefed me the lawyers were only interested in their fees, and I made statements to Parliament on that basis.

‌



“I have since learned this was false, and not only were those lawyers keen to settle for the sake of their clients, but my offer was never even delivered."

‌



Family's heartbreaking plea 26 years after Vicky Glass found murdered in stream READ MORE :

Nuclear test veterans' medical records were gathered by secret government lab READ MORE :

View 3 Images Kevan Jones has alleged he was given a false briefing by civil servants (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

“Had my orders been followed, this would all have been put to bed for a reasonable sum. I’ve passed my papers to the Defence Secretary, and I think he should waive the MoD’s client privilege so all documentation and discussion about my settlement offer can be published.”

‌



Solicitor Neil Sampson was representing the 1,011 vets and widows affected by the scandal at the time Lord Beamish drew up the deal. Mr Sampson said the MoD had an offer to make “but before they would tell us, we had to agree to either recommend whatever it was or, if we rejected it, we could not tell our clients”.

He added: “I would have been struck off had I agreed. It was effectively torpedoed. It bought time for the MoD to lodge an appeal, and the case was later thrown out.”

View 3 Images Neil Sampson was representing affected families while Lord Beamish drew up the deal (Image: Steve Bainbridge)

Article continues below

The Mirror ’s Nuke Blood Scandal campaign uncovered evidence of a secret programme of blood tests on troops, hidden behind national security and now the subject of a fresh legal battle and a major crime review by police. Thames Valley Police confirmed it is considering new leads for a full investigation.

A spokesman said: “This is a very complex matter that is receiving our full attention. There are many multifaceted enquiries, which continue, to establish a full assessment of all the facts that have been presented initially and more recently through several sources.”

An MoD spokesman said work continued on addressing veterans’ concerns, and added: “As this work progresses our focus will be on transparency, accountability and building confidence among veterans and their families.”

News.title: Labour conference live - Mahmood says 'more to come' on RAF Fairford 'terror attack' as Burnham chairs COBRA meeting
News.content:
The Prime Minister told LBC this afternoon that he wanted to get the 'full picture' of what happened at the base, and added he would share more details about the upcoming meeting

The Prime Minister announced on the sidelines of the Labour Party Conference today that he would be holding a COBRA meeting to address the RAF Fairford incident, with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood confirming after that she expects there to be "more to say in the days to come".

The Home Secretary told a fringe event at the Labour Party Conference that the decision to bail the suspects was a police operational decision. The Home Secretary said: "You will have heard some news from counter-terrorism policing about the release under bail. These are investigations, these are matters for the police, they have got to take the lead on how they use all of the powers at their disposal in cases such as these, but the investigations are continuing.

"So there'll be more to say in the days to come, I'm sure, as how those investigations are progressing. I've just come from a Cobra meeting with other colleagues in government chaired by the Prime Minister, and everyone should know that we are focused on this. You shouldn't read anything into the fact that we're limited in what we can say publicly at this stage except for the fact that nobody wants to compromise any investigation or any future court cases either."

Speaking with LBC's Shelagh Fogarty from Liverpool this afternoon, Andy Burnham said the security situation will be on the minds of many Brits following the arrests of five men in the nearby village of Whelford on on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences on Sunday. He told LBC that he wanted to get the “full picture” on what had happened at the base used by the British and US air forces in Gloucestershire.

Earlier, Wes Streeting gave an update on Britain's national security after five men were arrested over an alleged terror plot at an RAF base. The Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, said our response to any attempt to destroy a two-state solution in the Middle East would be: "we will not let you succeed"

And Chancellor John Healey set out plans to reindustrialise Britain with investment in industry and support for apprenticeships - while pledging that getting young people back into work was not just an "economic must" but a "moral duty". The Chancellor used his speech to the Labour Party conference to seek to reassure financial markets with a commitment to being responsible with the nation’s finances

News.title: Family's new garage blocked by council because it 'spoiled view for train passengers passing at 90mph'
News.content:
Family's new garage blocked by council because it 'spoiled view for train passengers passing at 90mph'

Planning officers said the proposed garage would have significant visual impact because it sits beside a protected landscape, a public footpath and the busy Cardiff to Manchester rail line

View 3 Images Thomas had already begun the works before they were halted (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

A family has been blocked from building a new garage after planners warned it could spoil views from trains speeding past their home at up to 90mph.

‌



The unusual objection was raised over plans at Tram Cottage in Llanfrechfa, near Cwmbran, where homeowner Thomas Hillier hopes to complete a garage beside the family home. A base has already been built and a canopy put up, but work was halted while the development went through the planning process.

‌



Thomas applied to Torfaen Borough Council for permission to retain the work already carried out and finish the garage, which would also include a first-floor home office. He also wants to change the use of the land from agricultural to residential.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas now has the right to appeal the refusal to a government planning inspector. (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

British resident slips from top of waterfall and plunges to her death in front of horrified friend READ MORE :

But planning officers recommended the scheme be refused, citing concerns about the effect on the surrounding countryside, the nearby public right of way and views from the railway line. The main Cardiff Central to Manchester Piccadilly line runs behind the rural property, with trains reaching speeds of up to 90mph on the route.

The line also carries thousands of commuters between Cwmbran, Newport and Cardiff. Tram Cottage sits within the South Eastern Lowlands Special Landscape Area and a protected green wedge, where development is tightly controlled.

‌



Planning officer Mia McAndrew said the site was at the end of a private lane and away from the public highway, but remained in a “sensitive” location under local and national planning policies. She stated: "The site is part of the special landscape area and immediately visible from the train line and a public right of way. Any visual impact from the proposed development is therefore considered to be significant.”

View 3 Images Drawings showed plans for a double garage with a space above which could be used as an office space (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

‌



Her report said development in the green wedge could only be permitted in limited circumstances. Ms McAndrew said: “This development goes beyond this, sprawling into surrounding countryside land.

"The applicant’s ownership of the land does not automatically change the use to residential. It is also considered that this minor residential development only benefits the occupant and would not have a community value to help justify any impact on the countryside, green wedge or special landscape area.”

The application was also criticised for failing to provide enough information about how the ecological impact of the development would be managed. Planning officers said the proposed size and siting of the garage would also harm the character of the surrounding area.

Article continues below

Thomas now has the right to appeal the refusal to a government planning inspector.

News.title: Dad and daughter, in her 20s, killed in same 'devastating' workplace incident
News.content:
Dad and daughter, in her 20s, killed in same 'devastating' workplace incident

A man in his 50s and his daughter in her 20s died following a tragic incident in Co Offaly, Ireland, with the company describing the tragedy as 'unprecedented'

View 3 Images The tragic incident happened at Banagher Precast Concrete in Co Offaly

A father and his daughter have both been killed in a horrific workplace tragedy, leaving a tight-knit workforce devastated and in a state of shock.

‌



The man, in his 50s, and his daughter, in her 20s, lost their lives following the incident at Banagher Precast Concrete, Co Offaly, in Ireland, shortly before midday on Monday, September 28.

‌



It is understood the pair are from Romania and had been employed at the Banagher plant for several years. Their deaths have plunged both stunned colleagues and the wider local community into mourning, with the company describing the incident as "unprecedented" and "devastating tragedy."

‌



Gardaí and emergency services raced to the scene at around 11.40am, where the man and woman were pronounced dead, reports the Irish Mirror.

The bodies of the victims were then transferred to Midlands Regional Hospital Tullamore, where post-mortem examinations are due to take place.

View 3 Images The bodies were taken to Midlands Regional Hospital Tullamore (Image: "irishphotos@mirror.co.uk" )

‌



Banagher Precast Concrete described the incident as "a devastating tragedy for everyone connected with our company", adding that employees were "all in deep shock".

In a statement issued to RTE News, the company said its Board of Directors, management team and staff offered their "deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences" to the families, friends and colleagues of those who perished.

The firm's immediate priority, it stressed, was providing support to the families of the two employees who died. Banagher Precast Concrete also took the opportunity to thank the emergency services and all those who responded to the incident. The full circumstances surrounding the tragic incident have yet to be established.

‌



The company said it would work fully alongside all statutory bodies and offer whatever support is needed as part of the ongoing investigation. The firm stated that the welfare of its workforce has always been a fundamental value, deeply ingrained within its day-to-day operations.

It described an incident of this magnitude as "unprecedented" for the organisation, adding that its employees were "all in deep shock".

The company has urged that the privacy of the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives be respected, and confirmed it would not be releasing any further details at this time.

‌



View 3 Images Tony McCormack TD , Offaly (Fianna Fail)

Fianna Fáil Offaly TD Tony McCormack extended his condolences following the devastating news.

"I was deeply saddened to hear the tragic news coming from Banagher, where two lives have been lost in a workplace incident," he told the Irish Independent.

Article continues below

"My thoughts are first and foremost with the families and loved ones of those who have lost their lives. I can only imagine the shock and heartbreak they are experiencing.

"I am also thinking of their friends, work colleagues and the wider Banagher community at this incredibly difficult time. My deepest sympathies go to everyone affected by this terrible tragedy."

News.title: Evri trials new delivery robots in Barnsley as it rolls out futuristic two-legged wheeled couriers
News.content:
Evri trials new delivery robots in Barnsley as it rolls out futuristic two-legged wheeled couriers

British delivery firm Evri is testing new delivery robots with advanced suspension 'legs' and a wheeled base designed to take them up stairs and over difficult terrain

View 4 Images Evri is trialling robots that look like they were designed by Wallace and Gromit (Image: Evri)

Two-legged delivery robots plucked straight from Wallace and Gromit could soon be delivering parcels to front doors across the country, if Evri get its way.

‌



The UK-based delivery firm has launched a trial of bipedal, wheeled robots as delivery workers today after partnering with Refined Robotics, a Japanese tech firm. The trial, which is underway in Barnsley, will see robots that look like a pair of the Wrong Trousers or Disney Pixar's famous bouncing lamp bring packages to real life Evri customers.

‌



The trial started this morning, and could see the newly designed robots enter the fleet alongside the existing crop of flagged, four-wheeled units already tasked with rolling deliveries to people's front doors.

‌



Diesel prices hit a record high - with warning of worse to come READ MORE :

13 UK areas may face Royal Mail delays - full list READ MORE :

View 4 Images Evri launched the trial this morning (Image: Getty Images)

The two-wheeled and legged new robots are meant to allow superior balance for the drones over potentially tricky terrain while travelling across neighbourhoods. They can travel at a record-breaking speeds of up to four miles an hour - around six kilometres an hour - and can hop out of vans before hauling their payloads straight to people's homes.

They are able to haul especially heavy parcels thanks to their "legs", which provide advanced suspension carrying up to 15kg, even up stairs. They have been designed with a host of advanced, onboard sensors which allow them to operate autonomously, although they will be operated remotely during the trial.

‌



How the robot trialss pan out in Barnsley, which Evri has dubbed "the UK’s Tech Town" and a priority location for the trial, will guide how the company goes forward with its new robots. The firm said the trial will primarily assess "how advanced robotics could complement Evri's existing delivery network and support its mission to be the most convenient way to send, receive and return parcels".

View 4 Images The trial is not meant to replace delivery workers, with robots only designed to complete part of the process (Image: Getty Images)

Evri will spend the trial evaluating how the new robots perform in residential environments, and how they could support its operational efficiency, all the while maintaining customer service standards. Nick Hafner, the CEO of Refined Robotics, said the firm was inspired to develop the new units after he saw an elderly driver carrying heavy parts up the stairs to his apartment during a heatwave.

‌



The firm says humans will still need to complete most difficult delivery routes and carry packages across ground the robots can't. He said: "Our two-legged delivery robot has been specifically designed to tackle some of the most complex challenges in last-mile logistics.

"Its ability to navigate stairs, uneven surfaces and outdoor environments makes it uniquely suited to supporting parcel delivery operations in real-world settings. We're delighted to partner with Evri on Europe's first trial of the technology and look forward to understanding how robotics can complement existing delivery networks and support the future of parcel delivery."

View 4 Images How the robots perform in Barnsley will inform how Evri proceeds with its plans (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Marcus Hunter, Chief Technology Officer at Evri Group, added: "At Evri, we're focused on giving customers more choice, convenience and control over how they receive their parcels. As the UK's leading parcel delivery company for delivery choice, we're continually exploring new technologies that can help us deliver even greater flexibility while maintaining the high-quality service our customers expect.

"Launching Europe's first trial of a two-legged delivery robot in Barnsley is an exciting milestone. Barnsley has built a reputation as a place where innovation thrives and new technologies can be tested in real-world environments. Our couriers remain at the heart of our business.

"We’re committed to exploring how innovation can support them, improve operational efficiency and help us continue offering customers even more choice, convenience and control in the future."

News.title: Trump 'surprised' RAF Fairford 'terror plot' suspects freed on bail - 'wouldn't have done it'
News.content:
Trump 'surprised' RAF Fairford 'terror plot' suspects freed on bail - 'wouldn't have done it'

Five men - all British nationals - detained over the suspected terror plot at RAF Fairford have been released on bail pending further enquiries

View 2 Images Trump was surprised by the decision (Image: BONNIE CASH/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

US President Donald Trump has said he is "surprised" five suspects were released on bail over the suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford, used by the US air force, and added that he would not have done so.

‌



Speaking in the Oval Office, Trump said the alleged plot "might be" linked to Iran, and added: "I will tell you, I would have said 'Don’t let them have bail'."

‌



"I’m surprised that they released them. I wouldn’t have done that," he said. But he repeated his praise of the British police, saying: "They worked with us very closely. We know everything about them [the suspects]. We would not have released them."

‌



The five suspects were arrested in the early hours of Sunday on suspicion of explosives offences and terrorism after three vans were seen near RAF Fairford, which has been used by the US to bomb missile sites in Iran.

They are a 24-year-old from Camden, north London; three men aged 23, 24 and 25 from Westminster, central London, and one aged 24 from Willesden, north-west London. Their release took place following "extensive interviews and inquiries".

View 2 Images Armed police at RAF Fairford after the discovery of the suspected plot (Image: Getty Images)

‌



UK's counter terrorism policing head, Lawrence Taylor, said: "To be very clear, this does not mean that the investigation is over. They are subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others. They absolutely remain under investigation as we explore multiple lines of inquiry."

It's understood that no explosive devices or materials were found in any of the vans. Iran said it "categorically rejects" that it had any involvement in the suspected RAF Fairford 'bomb plot', its London embassy has said in a statement.

Mr Taylor added: "Be assured, we are considering this from every possible angle, including that this may be actively committed by proxies or individuals, either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state."

‌



The possibility of a foreign state being behind he suspected attacks is still investigated, the chief said. The Gloucestershire base has been at the centre of protests against the government's decision to allow the US to use it to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sires that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards had warned Britain earlier in the year not to allow US bombers to fly from the base. Gloucestershire Police were initially alerted to three suspicious vans travelling towards the base at 12.45am on Sunday.

The vehicles were then spotted just under an hour later by a farmer who rang 999 fearing the men were involved in crime. Residents across around 85 households who were evacuated near the base have now been allowed to return home.

Article continues below

A cordon remains in place around three vehicles, Gloucestershire Police said.

News.title: Five men arrested in RAF Fairford incident released on police bail
News.content:
Five men who were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences near RAF Fairford are being released on police bail, counter-terror police have said.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) said officers were exploring "multiple lines of inquiry", including whether proxies or individuals working on behalf of a foreign state were involved.

The five men are all UK nationals in their 20s from London.

They were initially detained on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act and then further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.

Counter-terror police said they remained under investigation and their release was "subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others".

Three of the men live in Westminster, one in Camden and another in Willesden, police said, and they are aged between 23 and 25.

A farmer who called 999 to report the three white vans in the village of Whelford, which lies directly east of the base, told the BBC it was "pure luck" that she spotted them.

The woman, who wished to remain anonymous, said she arrived home to find the driveway and road blocked and saw a "large group of hooded and masked men".

"When they saw me they ran ahead of me - some into the field and some towards the neighbouring village of Kempsford. I then realised that something highly unusual was taking place," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

She said that she called the Ministry of Defence police at RAF Fairford but received no answer. She then rang 999 at 01:36 BST and said "within 10 minutes the village was full of armed police".

"I believe that my 999 call foiled whatever plans they had," she added.

News.content:

The men, UK nationals in their 20s, were arrested under the Explosives Act and on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.
