World.title: Costa Rica Turns to Bryan Ruiz After Firing Fernando Batista
World.content:
Former Costa Rica captain Bryan Ruiz will take temporary charge of the national team after the Costa Rican Football Federation fired Argentine coach Fernando Batista following a disastrous start to the Concacaf Nations League. The federation announced today that Batista and his coaching staff had been removed and that Ruiz would lead La Sele for its two remaining Nations League group matches. Costa Rica travels to Managua to face Nicaragua on Thursday, October 1, before returning home to play Haiti at Ricardo Saprissa Stadium on Sunday, October 4.

The move comes after Costa Rica lost its opening two matches of the competition, falling 4-3 at home to Curaçao on Thursday and then losing 2-0 to Haiti in Kingston, Jamaica, on Sunday. Those defeats ended Batista’s short and unsuccessful spell in charge. He coached Costa Rica in six matches without recording a victory, finishing with one draw and five losses. The team scored four goals and conceded 19 during that stretch.

Batista had been brought in earlier this year as Costa Rica attempted to rebuild following its failure to qualify for the 2026 World Cup. But the results never arrived, and the back-to-back Nations League defeats ultimately convinced federation officials to make another coaching change.

Ruiz, one of the best-known players in Costa Rican soccer history, now steps into the job with only a few days to prepare for Nicaragua. The former national team captain played a central role in Costa Rica’s historic run to the quarterfinals of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, scoring the winning goal against Italy and another against Greece in the Round of 16.

His coaching experience remains limited, although he recently got an early taste of managing at the senior level with Liga Deportiva Alajuelense. Ruiz took temporary control of the club following the departure of Ismael Rescalvo and won both matches he coached before returning to his previous role with Alajuelense’s under-20 team.

The federation has made clear that Ruiz’s appointment with the national team is also temporary. He will oversee the matches against Nicaragua and Haiti before officials begin the process of choosing a permanent coach for the road toward the 2030 World Cup.The immediate challenge is stopping one of Costa Rica’s worst runs in recent memory.

La Sele has now gone 350 days without a victory. Its last win came against Nicaragua on October 13, 2025, during World Cup qualifying. Since then, Costa Rica has gone eight consecutive matches without winning, a stretch that has included qualifiers, friendlies and Nations League games.

That makes Thursday’s match particularly significant. Ruiz’s first game in charge will come against the same opponent Costa Rica defeated the last time it celebrated a victory. Kickoff against Nicaragua is scheduled for 8 p.m. Costa Rica time at the National Stadium in Managua. Ruiz will then make his home coaching debut three days later when La Sele faces Haiti at 6 p.m. at Ricardo Saprissa Stadium.

World.title: New STEAM pavilion coming soon for Bishop Martin High School
World.content:
New STEAM pavilion coming soon for Bishop Martin High School

By Zoila Palma: Ground was officially broken today for a new STEAM Pavilion at Bishop Martin High School in Orange Walk Town, aimed at expanding opportunities for students in science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics.

The new facility will feature a fully equipped science laboratory, an engineering makerspace and a modern recording studio, providing students with spaces to develop practical and creative skills.

The project is supported through a national partnership between the Government of Belize, the Inter-American Development Bank and the Global Partnership for Education through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science and Technology’s Skills for the Future Program.

World.title: Belize City woman reported missing
World.content:
Belize City woman reported missing

By Zoila Palma: The family and friends of Belize City resident Ashema Chang,26, is concerned about her whereabouts.

She was last seen on September 22, 2026.

Anyone with information on her whereabouts is urged to call Crime Stoppers at 922, use the P3 app, or report to the nearest police station.

World.title: Prime Minister to Jules: “Attack me not my wife”
World.content:
Prime Minister to Jules: “Attack me not my wife”

By Zoila Palma: Today, Prime Minister John Briceno responded to the reports made over the weekend that his wife, Special Envoy for the Development of Families and Children Rosanna Briceno was in Guatemala following a recent incident involving Guatemalan military aircraft in Belize airspace.

“He can be an asshole with me, that’s fine but not my wife. Leave my wife out of this. When it came to this trip, she asked me and said John do you think I should go to Guatemala, I said yes because you are not invited as a state of Guatemala, you are invited to represent the country Belize, she was invited being the wife of the Prime Minister, so she was there representing Belize,” the Prime Minister explained.

PM Briceno added that while the Special Envoy was in Guatemala, the President apologized and implied that at times, there are people within the military that want to do as they wish.

“So, I want Jules Vasquez to understand this, leave my wife out of this, attack me not my wife,” the PM said.

World.title: Prime Minister: “What Guatemala has done is unacceptable”
World.content:
Prime Minister: “What Guatemala has done is unacceptable”

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño today announced that Belize Ambassador to Guatemala Jose Alpuche will be called home for consultations following the recent incident involving a Guatemalan military aircraft in Belizean airspace.

Briceño said he would meet with the Foreign Minister and the National Security Council this week.

“I will be meeting with the Foreign Minister and National Security council and then, one I would recommend that we call in the Ambassador from Guatemala in Belize for an explanation as to what is going on and to recall our Ambassador,” Briceño said.

“What has been done is unacceptable and as I said in my speech at the UN, that it seems that the Guatemalan military is trying to play some kind of games as we go into the ICJ. Try to destabilize this process and we will not allow that to happen. We will be talking to the friends of Belize, Americans, British, Canadians and OAS for them to understand that what Guatemala has done is unacceptable,” the Prime Minister added.

Briceño also emphasized the importance of diplomatic conduct between neighboring states. “This is not how democratically elected countries behave or how good neighbors behave,” he said.

World.title: Fans dub him ‘Stig Di Takis’ after explicit video goes viral
World.content:
Fans dub him ‘Stig Di Takis’ after explicit video goes viral

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Facebook was buzzing last night after a sexually explicit video allegedly featuring Belizean artist Stig Da Artist began making the rounds online. Stig has since fired back with a diss track aimed at his detractors, making serious allegations of his own and including lyrics that appear to contain threats of violence.

Stig quickly became the subject of countless jokes and memes online after a TikTok Live panel hosted by Giles, and featuring Corinth from TLC’s 90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days, discussed the video and spilled plenty of tea.

Corinth is no stranger to the drama surrounding Stig. She previously appeared on 90 Day Fiancé as a relative of Stig’s former girlfriend, Aviva, and was among those who confronted him on the show over allegations that he had been involved with other women while dating Aviva — allegations Stig denied.

The TikTok Live reportedly drew more than 300 viewers at one point. Members of the panel allegedly later circulated the explicit video in a WhatsApp group chat, helping fuel its rapid spread across Belizean social media.

Stig’s 90 Day Fiancé ex, Aviva, was also present in the livestream and was invited to join the panel, joking, “this is too messy but y’all funny.” The live at various points also featured popular Belizean social media personalities including Ivey Prada and Urlese Belizean Gill.

The discussion had viewers in an uproar, with some jokingly renaming the artist “Stig Di Takis” in reference to the graphic nature of the video and the online reaction to its contents.

The controversy also comes on the heels of the release of Stig’s new album, adding another layer to the sudden explosion of attention surrounding the artist.

Was it all an elaborate publicity stunt, or simply social media chaos taking on a life of its own? And should violent threats made in diss tracks be taken seriously?

Have you seen the video?

World.title: Lifetime’s ‘The Ocean Between Them’ puts Belize at center of dramatic sea survival story
World.content:
Lifetime’s ‘The Ocean Between Them’ puts Belize at center of dramatic sea survival story

By Zoila Palma: A family vacation in Belize turns into a terrifying fight for survival in Lifetime’s newest movie, “The Ocean Between Them”, which premiered Saturday night.

Inspired by actual events, the movie follows Miranda, a young kayaker who becomes stranded at sea after heading out alone following an argument with her mother, Joan. When a sudden storm strikes, Miranda is left battling dangerous ocean conditions and relying on her instincts to survive.

As Miranda struggles at sea, Joan refuses to give up on finding her daughter. The family’s vacation quickly becomes an urgent search, with Joan confronting her own physical and emotional limits while desperately trying to bring Miranda home.

The film follows both mother and daughter as they endure the ordeal from opposite sides—the daughter fighting the elements and the mother racing to find answers. The experience ultimately changes their lives as they fight to survive and reunite.

Rebecca Gayheart and Jessica Lord lead the cast, with Gayheart portraying Joan and Lord playing Miranda. Karl Walcott and Georgia Dane also appear in the film.

Belizean actors Wani Arzu, Adrian Garbutt and Jarell Velasquez are featured in the movie.

World.title: International News: Pope Leo urges Russia and Ukraine to pursue Peace talks
World.content:
International News: Pope Leo urges Russia and Ukraine to pursue Peace talks

By Zoila Palma: Today, Pope Leo XIV urged Russia and Ukraine to sit down for negotiations aimed at ending their four-year war, calling for dialogue and solutions that respect human life.

His comments came hours after he called on European leaders to be willing to make concessions in the interest of peace.

Speaking to reporters aboard his flight to Rome following a four-day visit to France, Pope Leo also expressed concern over growing discussions about nuclear weapons and increasingly destructive wars.

He said the Catholic Church has a responsibility to promote peace, human dignity and respect for life.

The pope called on leaders in Russia, Ukraine and other countries to engage in dialogue and seek ways to resolve disputes without continuing the conflict.

World.title: International News: Trump predicts US and Cuba will reach agreement
World.content:
International News: Trump predicts US and Cuba will reach agreement

By Zoila Palma: U.S. President Donald Trump said Saturday that he expects the United States and Cuba to reach an agreement and indicated that military action would not be necessary. “I would say that Cuba and us will make a deal. I don’t think we’ll need the military,” Trump told reporters at the White House.

Trump said the United States wants to help Cuba and “open Cuba up to our people.”

His comments came days after he described Cuba as a failed state during an address to the United Nations General Assembly and said that “freedom will be coming” to the island. The Cuban delegation walked out during his speech.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez later said Cuba remains open to dialogue and commercial and business relations with U.S. companies, while strongly condemning the longstanding U.S. trade embargo.

The United States has maintained the embargo for more than six decades.

World.title: Wolmer’s Boys student dies after collapsing during class
World.content:
Wolmer's Boys School Gate file photo

KINGSTON, Jamaica — A fourth-form Wolmer’s Boys High School student has died following a medical emergency at the school on Monday, the school has confirmed.

In a statement, the Wolmer’s Joint Board of Management indicated that the student collapsed during class and was rushed to hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

The board expressed profound sorrow at the passing of the young man, describing it as a deeply painful loss for his family and for the entire Wolmer’s community.

“The Joint Board extends its heartfelt condolences to his parents, relatives, friends, classmates, teachers and all whose lives he touched,” the statement read.

The school said it is providing support to affected students and members of staff and urged the public to refrain from circulating unverified information concerning the circumstances of his passing.

World.title: Lt Stitchie, dancehall icon who found new calling in gospel, dies at 60
World.content:
Lieutenant Stitchie (Photo via Instagram)

Veteran deejay Lieutenant Stitchie has died.

Observer Online understands that the entertainer, whose given name was Cleveland “Cleve” Laing, died at hospital on Monday, just one day before he would have celebrated his 61st birthday.

The tragic news comes less than 24 hours after the entertainer’s wife, Sophia Laing confirmed that he had been hospitalised with a low blood count and was receiving treatment at the Kingston Public Hospital.

READ: Lt Stitchie hospitalised with ‘low blood count’

The pioneering dancehall entertainer whose career spanned the formative years of the genre before he made a transition to gospel music, had been ailing for some time. His health issued stemmed largely from a debilitating stroke in the first week of September 2024.

Stitchie emerged from the competitive sound-system culture of Spanish Town in the early 1980s, working alongside figures including Papa San, Wickerman and Major Worries. His breakthrough came in 1986 with the humorous Wear Yuh Size, followed by Natty Dread, before his career expanded internationally with a recording deal with Atlantic Records in 1988.

But perhaps the most defining chapter of Stitchie’s life came when he left secular dancehall behind and devoted himself to ministry after becoming a born-again Christian in 1997. He subsequently built a thriving career in gospel reggae as his transition did little to diminish the respect he commanded within the wider entertainment fraternity.

His death is expected to reverberate across both communities, with artistes who shared stages, sound systems and recording studios with him likely to reflect on the contribution of a man who managed to reinvent himself without losing his place in Jamaican music history.

World.title: Jamaica has second-longest work week in the Americas, longest in Caribbean — report
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaica has been listed as the country with the second-longest average work week in the Americas and the longest in the Caribbean for 2026, according to a report shared by the World Population Review.

Eclipsed only by 28th-placed Honduras, whose population works an average of 44.20 hours per week, Jamaica placed 35th on the list, with locals working an average of 43.45 hours per week.

Men put in slightly more time than women, with their average listed as 44.55 and women at 42.14 hours per week.

Guyana was directly below Jamaica in 36th spot, with its population spending an average of 43.29 hours at work per week; far down the list at 61, with an average of 41.46 hours per week, was Haiti.

The three countries outpaced the global average of 38.67 hours per week.

The report, which relies on data collected by the International Labour Organization (ILO), noted that higher-income countries with a cultural emphasis on work/life balance generally have shorter official work weeks compared to countries with longer work weeks and rank higher on the world’s happiest countries list.

In contrast, countries with a longer work week, while often ranking as hard-working countries, usually have fewer worker protections, reduced amenities and a populace that is less happy and possibly overworked.

The Caribbean country with the shortest average work week was Barbados, with 34.47 hours per week on average.

With a 31.86-hour weekly average, Canadian citizens were listed as having the shortest work week in the region of the Americas, while the shortest globally was Yemen at an average of 22.95 hours per week.

World.title: Jamaica welcomes first cohort of Ghanaian healthcare workers
World.content:
Forty-three Ghanaian specialist nurses arrived in Jamaica.

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaica on Monday welcomed the first cohort of Ghanaian healthcare workers as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce and support the delivery of quality healthcare services.

The majority of the 43 nurses will be assigned to the Western Regional Health Authority (WRHA), which manages health facilities in St James, Westmoreland, Trelawny and Hanover and the South East Regional Health Authority (SERHA), which oversees Kingston & St Andrew, St Thomas and St Catherine.

The nurses, who are specialists in various areas, including critical care, paediatrics, operating theatre, nurse/midwife, emergency, oncology and mental health/psychiatric, will also serve in the other two health regions and at the University Hospital of the West Indies (UHWI).

Their arrival follows the signing of a Bilateral Health Cooperation agreement between the two countries earlier this year, which aims to place 400 healthcare workers in Jamaica.

“We warmly welcome the Ghanaian nurses and look forward to the valuable contribution they will make to our health system and the people we serve. This is not only in keeping with our Vision for Health 2030 plan but is fully aligned with the Ministry of Health & Wellness Jamaica’s Human Resource for Health (HRH) Stabilisation Strategy,” said Minister of Health & Wellness, Dr Christopher Tufton in a statement on Monday.

The ministry said the four-year agreement between Jamaica and Ghana has established a structured framework for the voluntary recruitment and temporary deployment of Ghanaian health professionals, particularly nurses and doctors, to support Jamaica’s healthcare system while promoting bilateral cooperation and ethical international recruitment practices.

It added that Jamaica and Ghana will further strengthen their partnership in health through additional technical cooperation in areas such as primary care reform, national health insurance and management of non-communicable diseases, among others.

World.title: Defence attorneys to withdraw services from courts islandwide Monday
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Following unsuccessful discussions with the Ministry of Justice, defence attorneys have been directed to withdraw legal services from all criminal courts islandwide on Monday as clashes over minimum mandatory sentences in the Firearms Prohibition Restriction and Regulation Act 2022 continue.

The action is expected to affect Parish Courts, Circuit Courts and Gun Courts.

Another day of industrial action, specifically targeting the Gun Courts, is scheduled on Tuesday.

A joint statement from the Jamaican Bar Association (Jambar) and Advocates Association of Jamaica (AAJ) indicated that members had voted overwhelmingly in favour of withdrawing legal services this week.

The vote followed a silent protest on Thursday in front of the Supreme Court in downtown Kingston by association members, where they lobbied for a review of the mandatory minimum sentences applied to certain gun crimes in the 2022 law.

READ: Lawyers protest mandatory minimum sentences under Firearms Act

Maintaining that the legal fraternity does not oppose stringent measures against violent gun crime, it emphasised that the legislation as currently constructed contains structural gaps and rigid mechanics that undermine the broader legal framework.

They described “significant shortcomings, gaps and statutory weaknesses” impacting the justice system, including what the attorneys describe as the erosion of judicial discretion, the dismantling of guilty plea incentives and the practical friction with statutory sentencing discount frameworks.

A meeting was held with Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs Delroy Chuck on Thursday to address the issues, but the lawyers say those discussions concluded without any definitive legislative timeline to address their concerns.

READ: Chuck to meet with protesting lawyers over Firearms Act discontent

The associations, however, urged attorneys to manage urgent remand list matters, emergency bail applications involving juveniles or vulnerable persons, and time-sensitive constitutional applications in a manner that ensures no client’s fundamental rights are prejudiced during this period.

The associations say they are again calling for urgent and meaningful legislative amendments to ensure the justice system functions efficiently for all Jamaicans.

World.title: New boys Tru Juice beat Molynes to go top of JPL
World.content:
In this file photo, Tru Juice FC's Daniel Roberts attempts a shot as he is being closed down by Reno FC's Raheem Kerr in the semi-finals of last season's Jamaica Football Championship at Llandilo Sports Complex in Westmoreland. Tru Juice won the game on penalties after playing out a 0-0 regulation and extra time score. (Photo: Paul Reid)

KINGSTON, Jamaica – Promoted side Tru-Juice extended their strong start to the Jamaica Premier League on Sunday as they edged Molynes United 1-0 at Stadium East to take over the lead in the points table.

Tru-Juice are joined by Montego Bay United on seven points after the St James-based club ended Racing United’s perfect start, winning 1-0 in the first game of a double header at Drewsland.

Meanwhile, defending champions Portmore United made a winning start to their title defense, beating Humble Lion 4-1, while Mt Pleasant FA got their first win, beating Dunbeholden 2-0.

Cavalier FC outscored Arnett Gardens 3-2 while Waterhouse FC beat Treasure Beach FC 2-0 to win their second straight game.

At Stadium East, Daniel Roberts scored in the 62nd minute, his third goal of the season, to lead Tru Juice to their second win of the season. The newcomers have gone three games without conceding a goal.

Jourdain Fletcher scored his first goal of the season to give Montego Bay the win, firing a rebound past goalkeeper Aaron Ennis in the Racing goal in the 27th minute.

Waterhouse scored two quick goals in the first half as they continued their good start to the season. Colorado Murray in the 35th minute and Mario Simms in the 37th minute punished mistakes by the Treasure Beach defense but, despite creating a handful of scoring chances, were unable to add to their tally.

Cavalier FC held off Arnett Gardens 3-2 to win their first game at new home venue Turners Oval, after leading 2-0 after the first 20 minutes.

Jeovanni Laing scored a stunning goal from well outside the area, into the far left corner to give Cavalier the lead in the 14th minute and Luis Watson doubled the advantage in the 20th minute with a powerful shot from close range.

Arnett Gardens started the fight back when Giovanni Taylor, scored in the 26th minute before Jamone Shepherd pulled them level in the 70th minute, both scoring their third goals of the season.

Cavalier reasserted themselves, however, and took all three points when Adrian Reid converted a penalty in the 83rd minute.

It took Portmore just over 60 minutes to break down Humble Lion but, once they got the first goal, scored four in a 23-minute span with Tarick Ximines getting a double.

Ximines opened the scoring in the 64th minute with Stephen Young getting a second in less than a minute. Ximines then completed his brace in the 70th minute before Kemar Mullings managed to pull a goal back for Humble Lion, their first goal of the season. Tedj Bryan restored Portmore’s three goals lead, scoring in the 87th minute.

Mt Pleasant, who had failed to score in their first two games, both losses, scored two early goals, Trayvone Reid in the 17th minute and Nicholas Nelson in the 22nd minute, to hand Dunbeholden their third straight loss of the season.

Meanwhile, Tivoli Gardens and Chapelton Maroons played out a 1-1 draw at the Edward Seaga Complex with two veteran players getting on the scoresheet.

Leaunghn Williams gave Tivoli the lead in the 29th minute before Brian Brown equalised for Chapelton in the 40th minute.

Sunday’s Games-

Tivoli Gardens-1, Chapelton Maroons-1

Cavalier FC-3, Arnett Gardens-2

Portmore United-4, Humble Lion FC-1

Dunbeholden FC-0, Mt Pleasant FA-2

Molynes United-0, Tru-Juice FC-1

Racing United-0, Montego Bay United-1

Waterhouse FC vs Treasure Beach- 8:00pm

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Bad roads backlash
World.content:
Minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan addressing Jamaica Observer editors and reporters last Friday.

ARGUING that Members of Parliament (MPs) and the central Government are taking undeserved flack for state of roads which are the responsibility of the municipal authorities, minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan has urged Jamaicans to put the pressure where it rightfully belongs.

“That’s why I came up with the Jamaica Road Register…to empower citizens to know which road belongs to which entity. The Members of Parliament are more visible a lot of the times, they sit in Parliament, and people feel that they have better access to them, so they pressure the MPs… But Jamaica has 27,000 kilometres of roads and most of the roads are owned by parish councils [municipal corporations],” Morgan told the Jamaica Observer during a sit-down last Friday.

He pointed out that, while the central Government is responsible for only 5,000 kilometres of roads, it has fixed several roads that are outside of its remit.

“The challenge we have is that a lot of the municipal corporations — whether it be a resource issue or whether it be a lack of interest — are not keeping up their end of the bargain. As a minister, and as a Member of Parliament, I have been elected to be accountable, so when somebody comes to me and criticises me about Hagley Park Road or Spanish Town Road, I have to take responsibility.

“But I find that I’m not getting that from the parish councils. For example, most of the roads that the Government has fixed in Kingston and St Andrew are not NWA [National Works Agency] roads, they are KSAMC [Kingston and St Andrew Municipal Corporation] roads, and before this new Mayor [Andrew Swaby] came in, the Parochial Revenue Fund was about $700 million a year; it is now over $1 billion, and we have not seen a commensurate increase in the allocation for repairing roads,” Morgan charged.

According to Morgan, while it is agreed that neither the NWA nor the municipal corporations have all the resources needed to fix every road, the measurable outcomes of the resources that the corporations get are still not being manifested.

“It was only when I went public — I think it was a couple months ago — that the mayor [Swaby] decided to increase allocations to each councillor for road work. The mayor has been there for over two years. Why didn’t he increase the allocation?” questioned Morgan.

“We have so many instances where MPs come to me and say, ‘Minister, the people are complaining to me about the road,’ and when I go and look, it’s not NWA’s responsibility, it is local government. So you have to make a decision — Is local government going to step up and do their job? And when I say local government, I mean the municipalities, because if they are not willing to fix the roads, then give it to central Government,” Morgan stated.

Claiming that there have been occasions in which the NWA went to fix roads and the entity was written to and told by a mayor to, ‘Leave the road alone, it’s a parish council road,’ Morgan charged that there is a desire by municipal corporations to hold on to what they cannot manage, “and that doesn’t make any sense, because clearly you are demonstrating that a majority of the roads that people are upset about are not main roads”.

Morgan admitted that several major thoroughfares in the Corporate Area are in need of repair but argued that many, including South Avenue, Lindsay Crescent and Beechwood Avenue, are municipal corporation roads and are to be fixed by the KSAMC.

“Duke Street, where the grates that are falling apart and, damaging people’s tyres, those are not the responsibility of the National Works Agency, those are the responsibility of the municipal corporation and yes, there are some mayors, across the island who are trying their best, but I don’t believe, particularly the Kingston and Saint Andrew [Municipal Corporation] is trying its best.

“So my point is, hold me accountable for my responsibilities as an elected representative and as a member of the Cabinet who has been given the responsibility for roads, but also hold the other people who are also elected responsible. They campaigned and promised you manna from Heaven and all the wonderful things. They need to come and deliver, and it’s not just roads,” charged Morgan.

While encouraging Jamaicans to use the JamaicaRoadRegister.gov.jm portal to see which roads are the responsibility of their local authorities and which are not, Morgan expressed hope that the soon-to-be introduced One Road Authority will make municipal corporations more accountable.

“It is not the intention of the One Road Authority to disempower municipal corporations, it is to give them tools and give citizens tools to hold both central government and local government accountable.

“For example, the people who throw the things on the road off the trucks, the trucks that are driving without cover, the people who are letting go water on the road, destroying the road, the cement trucks, the people who are digging up the road to run pipes and don’t fix it back, the developers who have destroyed most of the roads in Kingston with the sewage pipes that were not installed properly, those are things that disrespect the taxpayers of Jamaica, and those are things by next year will come to an end, because not only will the One Road Authority be able to find people, but the One Road Authority will also be able to go to court, and sue,” Morgan explained.

“We are going to take on the people who are destroying our roads and hold them accountable, because a lot of the damage to our roads is not necessarily because the road wasn’t fixed good, but because of the usage patterns of people who have the overweight trucks; your truck is supposed to only carry 80 tonnes, but you have 120. Our roads were not made for 120 tonnes.

“So we are thinking of working with Minister [of Transport Daryl] Vaz. I know that he’s working on bringing back scales, and it’s not just scales that are put down one place, I know that he’s planning mobile scales… You go to St Thomas, Paul Bogle Highway and it’s sand and gravel thrown away all over the road, and nobody wants to take responsibility. So, if the cement industry, the haulage industry, and other industries that use the road do not wish to voluntarily regulate themselves, then the Government has no choice but to regulate them,” said Morgan.

He added: “So what is going to happen is that we are going to impose harsh penalties on these companies, and it is not going to be the $300,000 that is in the Road Traffic Act — that is not being enforced — it is going to be worse because the One Road Authority is going to have its own enforcement officers.

“So it’s not police that is going to come and hold you accountable. The One Road Authority will have its own army of enforcement officers working with the police and others to show these people that the disrespect that they have shown to our roads cannot continue,” declared Morgan.

World.title: Alleged wife killer hospitalised after attack by jail inmates
World.content:
MONTEGO BAY, St James — A St James man accused of killing his wife has been hospitalised following an alleged attack by fellow jail inmates. Thirty-one-year-old Dane Watson was on Wednesday remanded in absentia after he failed to appear in court because of his injuries.

He is charged with the murder of 35-year-old Melissa Samnath, who was a Jamaican American living in New York.

Watson was scheduled to appear before St James Parish Court Judge Natiesha Fairclough-Hylton, but the court was informed that he was unable to appear. He is now scheduled to appear on October 8 when the judge is expected to examine the evidence already before the court and determine whether the matter should proceed to the Circuit Court.

Investigators told the court that Samnath was taken to Cornwall Regional Hospital on April 29 with multiple injuries and was later pronounced dead. Police allege that Watson transported her to the hospital, and then left the facility.

Investigators further allege that Watson subsequently left St James and was later located in Gayle, St Mary. Police said Watson contacted relatives because he was concerned about his safety. His relatives then alerted the Gayle police, prompting coordination between law-enforcement personnel in the two parishes.

Watson was eventually taken into custody and handed over to investigators in St James, where he was subsequently charged with murder.

According to media reports, Samnath was killed during what was a birthday trip to Jamaica. There were also reports that she realised she was in danger and sent text message to relatives who have played an active role in drawing public attention to the case.

World.title: Block US sanctions on ICC, EU lawmakers tell Commission
World.content:
U.S. sanctions on the ICC, which is based in The Hague, would present it with numerous operational challenges such as paying staff, accessing IT services and maintaining its detention facilities. The blocking statute could protect the court by preventing European companies from complying with U.S. sanctions.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on Monday visited the ICC in a show of support. His appearance was notable given Germany’s otherwise stalwart backing for Israel.

At a joint press conference with Wadephul, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen called the blocking statute the “nuclear option,” the AP reported. The Dutch government has been in touch with the Commission to ensure it can be quickly enacted, the Foreign Affairs Ministry told POLITICO.

French judge Nicolas Guillou, speaking at the economy committee hearing, said: “What’s at stake is whether we are going to be a democracy in the 21st century,” adding: “Will there be the rule of law in Europe?”

“We are in between terrorists from al Qaeda and Daesh, with some kleptocrats and some international drug traffickers in the same list.”

Guillou is one 13 ICC officials that the U.S. has sanctioned, including its president, Tomoko Akane of Japan.

World.title: Farage is still Labour’s main opponent, says party chair
World.content:
Pressed on the rising Tory threat, Phillipson told the “Politics at Sam and Anne’s” podcast: “I think history would show how electorally successful they are. But what I would say is that they have never reconciled with why they lost so badly in 2024.”

Donor move

Elsewhere in her POLITICO pub interview, Phillipson threw her weight behind moves to limit how parties can spend donations in the run-up to an election.

Labour is currently grappling with how to fight back against a mega-haul of donations to Reform from crypto entrepreneurs. There is currently no limit on the amount individual donors based in the U.K. can give to a political party, although donations above £11,180 must be reported to the Electoral Commission watchdog.

There is concern in Labour that a stringent cap could hit the governing party’s union funders, and Phillipson Monday that said she has “mixed views” on a policy to cap individual donations.

The equalities minister defended union cash in politics, arguing that “working people whose voices would not otherwise be heard” have the right to contribute.

But she said: “I’m more interested in how you make sure you regulate the spending rather than individual donations, because I think the latter is where we see increasing challenges around pushing the boundaries of the rules.”

World.title: Budget : le gouvernement envisage un gel “réversible” des retraites
World.content:
Finalement, un dispositif à trois étages est prévu par l’exécutif, mais sans graver dans le marbre le niveau des revalorisations.

“C’est une tentative très maline de résolution du problème dans lequel se trouvent les parlementaires, qui veulent tous geler [les pensions] mais pas le voter”, analyse une ancienne experte des comptes sociaux de Bercy.

Trois tranches, un décret

A l’approche de la présentation des textes financiers prévue jeudi matin, Sébastien Lecornu a promis qu’“aucune pension ne diminuera”, et que le “rythme d’augmentation [des retraites] sera tranché au Parlement”.

A ce stade, dans son projet d’article, le Premier ministre ne fixe aucun taux et laisse à son gouvernement (ou à un prochain exécutif en cours d’année) le soin d’ajuster le curseur.

Trois tranches sont retenues : jusqu’à 1260 euros, une revalorisation à l’inflation. Entre 1260 et 2034 euros, et au-delà de 2034 euros, le futur décret devra acter la sous-indexation, voire le gel des pensions.

“C’est réversible parce que le gouvernement pourra toujours changer le chiffre dans le décret”, relève un haut fonctionnaire consulté par POLITICO.

World.title: Labour conference: 6 things we learned down the POLITICO Pub
World.content:
1) Andy Burnham has some wind in his sails

Britain’s new PM goes into his big conference speech Tuesday with at least one reason to feel cheerful: he seems to have dramatically shifted the British public’s view of politics itself.

A majority of Brits say they believe his Labour Party has a real chance of winning the next election, whenever it comes. That’s the verdict of a new POLITICO Poll from Public First, unveiled at the pub Monday, and which captures the state of play after Burnham’s first two months as prime minister.

It found 53% of voters believe Labour has a realistic shot at keeping power. That is a big increase from 33% in May — when Starmer was in the final stages of his doomed premiership.

That was reflected in a bullish pub take from Lucy Powell, the Labour Party’s deputy leader. She told POLITICO she expects Labour to keep hold of the Holborn and St. Pancras seat at the upcoming parliamentary by-election triggered by Starmer’s exit from the political scene.

Caveat alert: Powell felt pretty chirpy about the Gorton and Denton by-election – where the party under Starmer lost to the Greens — too. So bookmark this one.

2) But Labour still has its eyes on Farage

Twelve months ago, all the main stage talk at Labour conference was about how Nigel Farage — then-ascendant in the polls — is a proper baddie.

World.title: Northern Ireland leader accused of joining ‘mob’ to block Protestant parade
World.content:
“Michelle O’Neill decided to follow the law of the mob and not the law of the land,” Little-Pengelly said in remarks directed at the Sinn Féin benches across the chamber.

Little-Pengelly accused O’Neill of standing “shoulder to shoulder” on the Garvaghy Road with senior members of the outlawed Provisional IRA, which has observed a cease-fire since 1997, and with leading Irish Republican Army dissidents who still plot bombings and shootings. “Sinn Féin are steeped in the history of murder … in the history of blood,” she said.

O’Neill shot back: “Why do the Orange Order, why do the DUP, why do unionism in general want to trample the rights of these people?” She said Portadown’s Catholics living along the Garvaghy Road “are entitled to live their life free from fear and intimidation.”

The planned parade, by 35 members of Northern Ireland’s main Protestant fraternal group, had been given legal sanction by the Parades Commission, an independent body tasked with minimizing conflict in a polarized society where Orangemen mount thousands of drum-thumping marches each year. The commission’s last-minute decision, after 28 years of refusals, thrilled the Democratic Unionists and shocked Sinn Féin.

Several hundred protesters — furious over the threatened reopening of a route that had triggered widespread violence in the mid-1990s, culminating in a 1998 ban — blocked the Garvaghy Road all night and refused to budge. Stuck in the middle between two stubborn camps, the Police Service of Northern Ireland decided not to confront the much larger group of protesters.

As Orangemen found their path eventually blocked by police armored cars, O’Neill gave an impromptu speech urging locals to keep blocking the road past midnight, lest the police perform an overnight U-turn and let the Orangemen through.

World.title: UK Treasury minister says her old job as City of London rep is ‘not a conflict’
World.content:
The City of London is lobbying hard against a windfall tax on the banks, as Labour seeks to balance the books.

Questioned on the departure from the U.K. of billionaire Chris Rokos — who pays £330 million a year in tax to the U.K. — Reynolds maintained that "we have to have rules."

"We want to create the very best conditions for growth, for entrepreneurship," she said. "But we have to have rules, and people who make a living here should pay taxes here."

The Treasury minister would not be drawn on the government-wide budget, which will be announced in October, but said ministers are "not powerless" in dealing with financial insecurity caused by international crises.

"We do face big global economic headwinds and a very difficult geopolitical situation with the ongoing war, particularly in the Middle East, but also in Ukraine," she said. "But we are not powerless to deal with those things, and we will do all that we can in the way that John [Healey] talked about earlier to further take further action to give families and businesses breathing space."

Intentions de votes à la présidentielle, résultats aux sénatoriales, enlisement du bloc central : tout semble rouler pour Marine Le Pen. World.title: Labour shouldn’t work with nationalists who want to break up the UK, says Welsh secretary
World.content:
Stephen Kinnock speaks at the POLITICO Pub at the Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, England on Sept. 28, 2026. | Baldo Sciacca for POLITICO

LIVERPOOL, England — Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock said Monday that Labour would struggle to work with Welsh nationalists Plaid Cymru after the next general election if no party wins a decisive victory.

Speaking at the POLITICO Pub at Labour Party conference, Kinnock said he “cannot see any circumstances where you could cooperate in any meaningful way, really, with a party that wants to break up the United Kingdom.”

Kinnock, who joined the Cabinet in July, said he does believe people in the center-left nationalist force “want what I want, which is the best for Wales.”

World.title: Sweden's Social Democrat leader Andersson says 'currently no possibility' to form government
World.content:
Sweden's Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson said she had failed to form a government with the country's election-winning centre-left bloc.

 

"I can conclude that there is currently no possibility for me to form a government," she told reporters on Monday, adding that she would inform the speaker of parliament that she was "returning the mandate entrusted to me."

Andreas Norlén, the speaker, announced that he would talk with party leaders on Wednesday as they work to find the most suitable candidate to attempt to form a government.

"I envision that after those deliberations, I will be able to return with new information on how the process will move forward," Norlén said.

Norlén, who was reelected as speaker on Monday, had given the task of trying to form a government to Andersson on 18 September.

Outgoing Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, who resigned in the wake of the election loss, is now expected to be asked to make an attempt.

Andersson's centre-left alliance holds a three-seat majority in Sweden's 349-seat parliament. The bloc, which also includes the Left Party, the Centre Party, and the Green Party, won a total of 176 seats in the Riksdag. Kristersson's right-wing bloc won 173 seats. The Social Democrats finished the election as the largest single party, winning 99 seats.

Following the election, Kristersson called for "constructive openness" across parties in order to work towards forming a government.

"Discussions will need to be held with all parties to find ways around these impasses and create the conditions for a stable and capable government," he said.

He is now believed to be looking to win over the Centre Party, which was once a part of the right-wing bloc.

However, its leader, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, has pledged to uphold centrist policies and has refused to support a government that gives influence to parties on the edges of the political spectrum.

In Sweden, if the speaker fails four times at getting their proposal for a prime minister approved by the Riksdag, then a snap election must be held.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV wraps up four-day France visit in the city of Metz
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV left for Rome on Monday evening after a historic four-day visit to France that sparked huge enthusiasm.

 

The American pope was escorted to the airport in the eastern city of Metz by President Emmanuel Macron, who saw him off after the pope wrapped up a trip that also took him to Paris and Lourdes.

"We're sad that he's leaving, but happy that everything went well," Macron said.

On Sunday evening, Macron reversed an earlier decision not to attend the Pope’s final Mass at Metz Cathedral. He had not been present for any of the Masses held during the pontiff's four-day visit.

France’s principle of "laïcité", which enshrines a strict separation between the Church and state, has previously sparked debate over whether the country’s head of state should attend a papal Mass.

An 'incredibly moving' visit for the faithful in Metz

Inès, who drove five hours from the northern French town of Rouen to see the Pope in Metz, told Euronews that she felt "incredibly moved" seeing him in his popemobile.

"I felt so emotional, it was truly touching. The fact that we were all able to come together in this shared experience, creating a sense of community, is very special", she said.

Meanwhile, sisters Antonia and Marie, who travelled from the wider area to see the Pope's parade, said that the messages he delivered about the importance of peace on the European continent, were deeply moving.

"In the times that the world is facing it made us feel heard and gave us hope to keep going."

World.title: National Rally's Bardella denies report he made antisemitic remarks
World.content:
Jordan Bardella is at the centre of a new controversy in France after an article published by Mediapart on Monday alleged that the president of the hard-right National Rally (RN) party had made antisemitic remarks early in his political career.

 

In the report, Mediapart alleged Bardella had made a number of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments in private conversations between 2013 and 2015.

Bardella celebrated his 18th birthday on 13 September 2013 and would go on to become the National Front's departmental secretary in Seine-Saint-Denis a year later.

The investigative outlet said it had found further exchanges in which Bardella promoted conspiracy theories targeting Jewish political figures or people believed to be linked to Israel.

In one of the conversations, he is reported to have said: "The Jew must dominate other peoples, crush them and rob them; a Zionist is necessarily a Jew, and one through and through.”

He is also reported to have stated: “And that is what they want: a New World Order dominated by Israel, with Jerusalem, of course, as its capital."

When contacted prior to publication, Bardella, according to Mediapart, "formally" denied the allegations.

In a post on X, Bardella also called the allegations "blatant fabrications."

"I formally refute the accusations levelled against me by Mediapart, which attribute to me delusional and antisemitic remarks that I allegedly made whilst I was a minor," he wrote.

"At a time when the victory of our ideas has never been so close, certain militant sections of the press are prepared to orchestrate smear campaigns to destabilise the presidential campaign and undermine my reputation," he continued, adding that he had instructed a lawyer to "take all necessary legal action against Mediapart."

Marine Le Pen has come to the defence of her protégé.

Whilst visiting a construction trade fair in Paris on Monday, she was asked about the article, saying that she could not "believe such nonsense" and accusing Mediapart of resorting to "dirty tricks" and "smear campaigns."

Edwy Plenel, a cofounder of Mediapart, said the article was the "result of an investigation lasting several months, based on dozens of written conversations – which we have been able to independently verify – drawn from a wider body of evidence, supplemented by witness accounts."

The allegations come as Bardella has emerged as one of the RN's leading figures and a close ally of Le Pen.

RN's leadership has for several years been making efforts to distance the party from a legacy marked by antisemitic comments from its founder, Jean-Marie Le Pen.

World.title: KIDS Act: Do Europeans support banning social media for children?
World.content:
A new EU proposal, the KIDS Act, could ban children under 13 from using social media and limit features for those aged 13 to 15.

 

The goal is to crack down on phone addiction and doomscrolling, but also to protect children from harmful content — or contacts — as well as mental and physical risks.

Child rights organisations have welcomed the move, though some are warning that restricting social media access to teenagers might push them towards even more dangerous online communities.

The vast majority of EU citizens (91%) agree that more measures are needed to regulate child social media use, according to Eurobarometer's poll EU Challenges and Priorities.

The action that received the largest support (36%) was a social media ban for children under a certain age.

Greece shows the strongest backing for this measure with 49%, followed by Bulgaria, Romania, Portugal, Ireland and Slovakia, all at 44%. The lowest support emerged in a cluster of central European countries: Austria (27%), Germany (28%), and the Czech Republic (29%).

'Shifting the burden from platforms to parents'

However, some child rights organisations are not too impressed with the EU's plan.

"We back 13 as the minimum age, but we don't see it as a new ban," Jeanne-Marie Quashie, EU advocacy officer at Terre des Hommes Netherlands, told Europe in Motion. "Currently, social media platforms have set 13 as the age to access their platforms."

She said that the act's age limit aligns with standards already set out in Article 8 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and that the new legislation needs improvement in how it intends to regulate access for 13- and 14-year-olds.

Under the current framework, teenagers won't be able to independently create a social media account, but their parents will have to initiate and confirm the account for them.

The account will then be managed through a linked parent profile or an admin dashboard, which will, for example, set the screen time limit, with a maximum of one hour per day.

In which case, a considerable part of responsibility will fall on parents.

"The EU KIDS Act is moving in the right direction by targeting platform design over blanket bans", Quashie said. "But making access depend on a parent's sign-up shifts the burden from tech companies onto families."

"For 13- to 15-year-olds, safety must be built in, not switched on," she added. "Children's access to online spaces must be conditional on safety, not parental authorisation."

Child social safety: What are Europeans most concerned about?

Concern about child social media use runs high across the EU, with around 70% of respondents saying they are very or somewhat worried about cyberbullying (71%), online grooming (70%), and exposure to harmful content (69%).

At the same time, concern about addictive design, one of the main targets of the KIDS Act, polled lower, at just 60%, with only 28% very concerned.

Yet there are some exceptions: in Cyprus, the rate of respondents worried about addictive design jumps to 89%, while it reaches 87% in Luxembourg.

World.title: Ukraine's city of Oleshky faces starvation as Russia blocks all aid
World.content:
Ukrainian forces have delivered around 4 tonnes of food to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region by drone in one of the largest such operations of the war, as roughly 2,000 remaining residents face what international organisations have described as a worsening humanitarian catastrophe.

 

Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022. No food has reached the city through regular channels since May of this year, according to ground reports.

Meanwhile, Russian forces are blocking civilians from evacuating and actively obstructing drone deliveries.

Oleksandr Prokudin, head of the Kherson regional military administration, said troops are shooting down food-carrying drones, confiscating or reselling supplies that reach the ground, and detaining residents found with humanitarian parcels.

Soldiers are conducting house-to-house searches for dropped food, residents report.

Ukrainian forces have been delivering aid by drone across the Dnipro since March, the regional administration said. The location and timing of individual operations are withheld for security reasons. Ukrainian troops hold positions on the right bank of the Dnipro, several kilometres from the city.

Thousands in peril of death

The regional military administration puts the population still in Oleshky at around 2,000, including nearly 50 children, down from 25,000 residents before Russia's all-out invasion in early 2022.

The All-Ukrainian Council of Churches and Religious Organisations estimates more than 6,000 people remain in the city and surrounding area, including around 200 children.

Ukrainian officials say anyone suspected of contact with Ukrainian authorities or armed forces faces immediate execution.

Conditions in the city have deteriorated sharply since the destruction of the Kakhovka hydroelectric dam in June 2023, which flooded large parts of the region, destroyed hundreds of homes and blocked wells and sewage systems. At least 200 to 300 people died in Oleshky in the flooding alone.

Residents now rely primarily on their own gardens for food, face chronic medicine shortages and move between abandoned buildings to avoid drone raids and looting by Russian troops, according to reports from the city.

"People are lying on the roads, rotting, unburied. Today in the basement of the hospital, the very one that has had no electricity for four years now, there are more than 100 corpses," Tetyana Hasanenko, an employee of the Oleshky city military administration, told ABC News.

The 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen," involved in the drone deliveries, published footage from the city in April that it described as showing a settlement Russian forces had "turned into a ghost town".

"People are forced to eat grass and weeds to survive. The roads are mined, it is almost impossible to get out safely, and shelling and drone attacks continue all around," Musician Artem Pivovarov said.

"There are reports that the bodies of those killed remain on the streets for months, there is no one to collect them."

Evacuation plan obstructed by Moscow

Kyiv has drawn up a humanitarian evacuation plan that the International Committee of the Red Cross is prepared to join.

Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said Russia has not confirmed its readiness to allow the mission to proceed. Without agreed access, volunteers cannot enter the city on their own.

Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has called on international organisations to secure humanitarian access.

"Russia is deliberately provoking a humanitarian catastrophe in the occupied part of the Kherson region. It is blocking access to food and medicine, obstructing the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of civilians, while Russian FPV drones hunt people in the streets," Sybiha said.

The UN mission in Ukraine described the situation in Oleshky as "desperate" in June, saying thousands of civilians faced "a serious threat to their lives, a lack of food and no access to medical care."

Michael O'Flaherty, the Council of Europe's Commissioner for Human Rights, said he was "alarmed by the rapidly worsening humanitarian crisis".

"Civilians, including children, are trapped without sufficient food, medicines, medical care, running water or electricity," O'Flaherty said in a statement.

"Reports indicate that they face a high risk of death."

O'Flaherty reminded Russia of its legal obligations: under international humanitarian law, the occupying power must ensure the population has access to food and medicines.

Ukrainian tennis player Oleksandra Oliinykova, ranked world number 47, drew public attention to the city on social media: "Please, google Oleshky. It is a town that is currently under temporary occupation. There is a humanitarian catastrophe there."

Ukrainian supporters displayed a banner reading "Save Oleshky" during a recent Hungary-Ukraine football match.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov acknowledged the situation in Oleshky was "indeed critical" but blamed the "Kyiv regime" for blocking deliveries.

Oleshky is not the only Ukrainian settlement rendered uninhabitable under Russian occupation or bombardment since February 2022.

Mariupol, a port city of around 425,000 people, was razed in a weeks-long Russian siege in spring 2022, while Bakhmut and Avdiivka in the Donetsk region were almost entirely destroyed before falling to Russian forces in 2023 and 2024, respectively.

Towns including Volnovakha, Rubizhne and Maryinka have been reduced to rubble along the frontline. Ukrainian authorities estimate more than 210,000 buildings have been destroyed across the country since the full-scale invasion began.

World.title: Houthi attacks put Turkey’s new Saudi defence pact to the test
World.content:
Attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia are putting Turkey's new defence pact with the kingdom to its first major test – forcing Ankara to weigh support for its ally against the risk of being drawn deeper into the conflict.

Advertising

Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on 7 August, committing themselves to the principle that an attack on one is an attack on all.

The three countries' military chiefs met in the Saudi capital on Friday, a day after the Iran-backed Houthis launched their latest barrage of missiles targeting Riyadh and Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Yanbu.

In recent weeks, Saudi Arabia has reported intercepting numerous Houthi drone and ballistic missile attacks from neighbouring Yemen.

The military chiefs discussed intelligence sharing, military coordination and integrating their capabilities, Saudi and Pakistani statements said. Turkey's defence ministry did not comment on the meeting.

Erdogan hints at larger nuclear partnership with Russia, unsettling Turkey's allies

Saudi expectations

Turkey has so far stopped short of committing itself to military action.

Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said this month that Ankara was looking into providing what he called “technical support”, without elaborating on what that could involve.

Saudi Arabia could look to Turkey for air defence systems, counter-drone technology, radars and maritime security, given the expertise and capabilities of the Turkish military and defence industry, said Amed Khuzaie of the Washington-based think tank N7 Foundation.

“The Mecca Agreement pact will prove its vitality and importance only if it's deemed to be functional,” Khuzaie told RFI.

The Riyadh meeting followed talks in New York on Thursday involving the Saudi and Turkish foreign ministers and Pakistan's deputy prime minister and foreign minister on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

Turkish media citing foreign ministry sources said the meeting focused on ongoing “technical negotiations”.

But providing support to Saudi Arabia could expose Turkey to retaliation from the Houthis.

“By God, if Turkey and Pakistan become involved, we will strike them with an iron fist,” Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a senior member of the Houthis, said in an Iraqi television interview.

Turkey seeks Black Sea shipping deal as attacks threaten grain trade

Risk of retaliation

The warning should be taken seriously given the Houthis' military presence around the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a critical waterway linking the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, explained Amed Nagi, a Yemen expert at the International Crisis Group.

“[The Houthis] targeted US and UK shipping in the Red Sea,” Nagi said. “They could do the same beyond [that] to the Gulf of Aden, because we know Turkey is very active in the Horn of Africa.

"So I think these are the areas that the Houthis will think about if there is any sort of retaliation against Turkey.”

In 2024, the Houthis attacked US military and commercial shipping in the Red Sea, damaging the Gibraltar Eagle bulk carrier with a cruise missile and sinking the British-linked cargo ship MV Rubymar.

Saudi Arabia could also look to Israel for support if its new partners do not provide what it needs, Khuzaie said.

“Who has better intelligence in the region than the Israelis today?” he said. “Diversifying resources, if one fails you, you have another side that could assist.”

The risks for Ankara go beyond possible Houthi retaliation. Turkey must also manage its relationship with Iran, which backs the Yemeni group.

“It is not in the interest of Turkey to have a direct confrontation with any actor in the region, and the Houthis have become a proxy of Iran; Turkey doesn't want a confrontation with Iran directly," said Bilgehan Alagoz, an international relations professor at Istanbul's Marmara University.

"Turkey is trying to solve the issue from a diplomatic point of view.”

In a joint statement last week, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt said that dialogue and diplomacy were the only sustainable way to resolve the region's conflicts, while affirming Saudi Arabia's right to defend itself under international law.

Fidan met his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in New York on Friday.

Fidan later said they discussed Iran's negotiations with the United States and conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but that diplomatic efforts had yet to produce a breakthrough.

What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey

Iran balancing act

The diplomatic efforts come as Turkey's relationship with Iran faces other strains.

Turkey-based international relations analyst Soli Ozel said Ankara has for decades walked a “fine line” between rivalry and cooperation with Tehran while balancing its relationships with Iran and Western allies, particularly the United States.

Turkey's banking regulator recently revoked the operating licence of Iran's Bank Mellat branch in Istanbul, although the official notice did not say the move was intended to enforce US sanctions.

The US Treasury also said Ankara had agreed after talks with Washington to stop flights by Iran's Mahan Air as part of efforts to comply with US measures against Tehran. Three Turkish airlines also suspended flights to Iran.

Turkish authorities have also repeatedly accused Iran of hostile operations inside the country, including assassinations and abductions of Iranian dissidents.

In January, security forces arrested six people suspected of spying for Iran and gathering information about the Incirlik air base, which is used by US forces.

Becoming involved in the conflict against the Houthis could upset Ankara's already delicate relationship with Tehran, Ozel told RFI.

“The Iranians who actually have a lot of [intelligence] capabilities in Turkey, we’ve seen that before, then you find yourself in a hot or cold war,” he said.

World.title: Iranian human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh wins the 2026 Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize
World.content:
The Council of Europe awarded human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh with the Vaclav Havel human rights prize. She is a prominent advocate for the rights of women, children and political prisoners.

Human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh is one of Iran's best-known human rights activists. On September 28, she was awarded the Council of Europe's Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize.

In 2026, Sotoudeh was one of three finalists for prize. The other nominees were the Iranian-American journalist and women's rights activist Masih Alinejad and the Hungarian human rights lawyer Marta Pardavi.

The Council of Europe is honoring Sotoudeh's longstanding commitment to human rights and her work, which she has carried out at considerable personal risk.

The council said Sotoudeh campaigned against compulsory hijab laws and the death penalty, "despite repeated arrests, lengthy imprisonment and great personal risk."

Who is Nasrin Sotoudeh?

Human rights lawyer Sotoudeh is committed to women's rights, the rights of political prisoners, and the abolition of the death penalty. She has represented numerous activists, journalists, members of religious minorities, and people sentenced to death.

"In moments like this, we remember past struggles, we recall our shared ideals and we think of the individuals across the globe who stand with us," Sotoudeh in a video statement from Tehran.

As early as 2012, she was awarded the European Parliament's Sakharov Prize, along with film director Jafar Panahi. At the time, she was in prison and was unable to accept the award in person.

In 2019, she had been sentenced to 33 years in prison and 148 lashes. One reason for the sentence was her work as a lawyer for women who had protested against Iran's headscarf mandate.

Even while in prison, she continued her advocacy for human rights. In 2020, Sotoudeh went on a hunger strike at Evin Prison to protest the conditions of detention and the situation of political prisoners. That same year, she was among the recipients of the Alternative Nobel Prize (Right Livelihood Award) and learned of the award while in prison.

Voice for women's rights in Iran

During Iran's nationwide "Woman, Life, Freedom" protest movement in 2022, Sotoudeh once again became a leading voice for the rights of Iranian women.

Iran uprising seen through the eyes of Iranian women To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Her decades-long commitment symbolizes the enduring resistance against state restrictions and repression. She has been arrested repeatedly and sentenced to long prison terms, including in April 2026. In May, she was released on bail.

The Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize recognizes "outstanding civil society action in defense of human rights" in Europe and elsewhere. The prize is worth €60,000 and is awarded by the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) in cooperation with the Charter 77 Foundation.

World.title: Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
World.content:
A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

Flight restrictions at Italy's Catania Aiport were extended on Monday, following disruptions to services over the weekend.

A thick ash cloud emanating from the nearby Mount Etna volcano has prompted authorities to halt flights.

What do we know about the disruption?

The Sicilian aiport's operator, SAC, said that all flight operations at the hub had been suspended until at least midnight local time (2200 GMT/UTC) on Monday night.

It said that where possible arrivals and departures were transferring to Sicily's other airports in Palermo and Comiso. Catania is Italy's fifth-busiest airport, and Sicily's largest hub.

Catania airport said that where possible, flights were diverting to Sicily's other airports, Palermo or Comiso Image: Salvatore Allegra/Anadolu/IMAGO

SAC advised passengers to check the status of their flights prior to setting off for the airport.

The Mediterranean island is a popular holiday destination but travelers have faced frequent disruptions this summer because of eruptions and more commonly because of ash emanating from Etna.

Ash from the northeast crater of the mountain is being carried southward by the wind.

Italian Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) said the ash did not appear to indicate an imminent explosive phase.

What is Mount Etna?

Mount Etna is a roughly 3,400 meter (roughly 11,100 feet) stratovolcano on Sicily's eastern coast. Its precise height is ever changing, particularly amid periods of high activity when it can shed a few meters.

The city of Catania is located not far to the south.

Despite the dangers, settling near volcanoes also has advantages like rich soil, hence Catania's success down the centuries Image: Salvatore Allegra/Anadolu/IMAGO

Etna is one of the tallest active volcanoes in Europe and Italy's highest peak south of the Alps.

It's in an almost constant state of low-level activity and erupts in a more pronounced manner fairly frequently. It has caused disruptions at Catania airport several times this year, and in recent years.

A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the first volcanic activity took place at Etna about half a million years ago.

Both Roman and Greek mythology asserted that the god of blacksmithing — either Vulcan or Hephaestus — had his forge beneath Mount Etna.

World.title: SpaceX launches supersized Starship into orbit
World.content:
Starship is the biggest and most powerful spacecraft ever built and it is meant to support NASA's Artemis moon program.

US airspace giant SpaceX on Monday launched its Starship spacecraft into orbit. The firm hoped the Starship could complete six full laps around Earth in order to prove its readiness for NASA's Artemis moon program.

"Starship is orbital," Mission Control announced to cheers. The Launch took place at Starbase, Texas. The laps were supposed to last around 10 hours, ending with a Pacific splashdown near Chile.

But just an hour after liftoff, SpaceX said it planned to bring Starship back to Earth after about three hours in orbit, cutting the 10-hour trip short.

Starship launches 26 satellites

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman praised SpaceX for reaching orbit and "managing every step in a safe, responsible and especially inspirational way."

Starship is the biggest and most powerful spacecraft ever built, it was propelled by a 407-foot (124-meter) rocket that was designed from the start to be fully reusable.

The spacecraft was loaded with 26 of the latest and most advanced Starlink satellites, which were released one by one, to join the 11,000 older models already providing internet service.

"All 26 Starlink V3 operational satellites deployed and operating nominally," SpaceX CEO ElonMusk wrote on X.

SpaceX's so-called V3 satellites are designed to unfold their antennas and solar panels after release before establishing connections with Earth and other Starlink satellites.

SpaceX began flying Starship in 2023 and the program has seen its successes and failures of successive tests. Technical challenges remain before Starship can fulfill its mandates, such as conduct commercial flights, deploy data centers in orbit or reach the Moon or the Red Planet.

World.title: Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
World.content:
Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

A Turkish comedian was convicted in Istanbul on Monday on charges of "insulting" President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and "insulting religious values" during a stand-up performance in June.

The judge provisionally sentenced Deniz Goktas to 19 months in prison, but ordered his release pending the judicial review and appeal process that would finalized the verdict.

It was not immediately clear how long this process might take.

NATO member and EU aspirant Turkey routinely tries people on speech-related offenses, particularly and famously when it comes to supposed "insults" of its longserving leader Erdogan.

What was the case about?

Deniz Goktas, 32, was arrested on July 3, a week after releasing a YouTube video of his show that was watched nearly 9 million times and a few days after shorter clips he posted on X enjoyed similar rapid success.

He faced an array of charges related to content in his "Dead Sea" show. Goktas referred to his impending court appointment online on Sunday, in one of his irreverent social media posts from his cell.

Goktas was accused of insulting Erdogan, of inciting public hatred and hostility — via jokes about Islam — and of praising crime and criminals, an additional charge added by prosecutors tied to a joke about an organized crime family, the Daltons

His trial is the latest in a widening crackdown on people seen as critical of Turkey's moderate Islamist government. Hundreds of politicians, artists, musicians, journalists and LGBTQ activists are among those to face detention or trial.

LGBTQ+ communities in Turkey fear intensifying clampdown To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What did Goktas say in his defense in court?

Goktas did not dispute the content from his popular show, but did argue in court that he had committed no crimes with his jokes.

Prosecutors had for instance singled out a pair of references he made to President Erdogan as a "dictator" as illegal insults.

"Dictator is not an insult: it is a political characterization," Goktas told the court. "As the president and leader of the party that has ruled the country for 25 years, a political comedy show in which Erdogan's name is never mentioned would be neither sincere nor have any connection to reality."

He said that Erdogan should be "open to the art of satire," as he said past presidents in Turkish democracy were.

"The joke hasn't changed. What has changed is the increasingly fragile leadership that can no longer tolerate the joke," he said.

The judge nevertheless convicted Gotkas of insulting Erdogan, and downgraded the charge he faced of "inciting hatred and hostility" with jokes about Islam, instead convicting him of the lesser supposed crime of "insulting religious values."

He cleared the comedian of the third charge of allegedly praising criminality.

Goktas has spent just under three months in pretrial detention, which should count as time served in any potential custodial sentence.

News of Goktas' arrest in early July prompted protest in Istanbul [FILE: July 3, 2026] Image: Yasin Akgul/AFP

Erdogan the only claimant, Diyanet religious authority among those to complain

According to the Turkish NGO the Media and Law Studies Association (MLSA) , prosecutors cited more than 500 applications to prosecute the performer regarding the show.

They were issued to the Presidential Communication Center that monitors such issues. One of the groups to provide a tipoff was the government-sponsored Presidency of Religious affairs, better known as Diyanet.

Erdogan, in charge of Turkey either as prime minister or later president since 2003, was named as the sole complainant.

His government has attracted attention in recent years for its prosecution of people deemed to have unfairly criticized the authorities, and for the various lawsuits against leading members of the opposition, particularly the CHP. The Turkish president's litigious streak also became headline news in Germany around a decade ago, when he pursued star TV comedian Jan Böhmermann.

Meanwhile the MLSA said that Goktas' jokes alleged to have the potential to "publicly incite hatred and hostility" took aim at fundamentalist Islam, including a reference to women in full-coverage swimsuits being "divers" and joking about "suicide bombers who fast."

Turkey nominally has a secular constitution and guarantees of free speech. However, the EU and the US have often criticized its application of these standards.

The US Commission on International Religious Freedom wrote in a 2022 report that Erdogan's government increasingly relied on speech-based prosecution to "silence individuals who express criticism in religious terms, disclose beliefs or a lack thereof that differ from those of the majority of the population, or engage with religion in a way perceived as 'mocking' or 'irreverent.'"
