World.title: Hungary’s largest bank OTP could quit Russia as potential new deal reshapes plans
World.content:
Hungary’s largest bank, OTP, is reviewing its strategy in Russia and is considering a complete withdrawal from the country, Chief Executive Officer Péter Csányi has told Bloomberg.

The review comes as OTP seeks regulatory approval for its planned acquisition of Baltic banking group Luminor, a deal that would significantly expand its presence in the euro area. OTP expects the review to be completed by the end of 2026, with the decision taking into account long-term shareholder value and the bank’s strategic commitment to the Baltic region.

Luminor deal sharpens focus on Russia

The Russian operation remains profitable. According to figures reported by Bloomberg, its profit reached approximately HUF 202 billion (about EUR 550.3 million) last year, having increased more than fivefold since 2021. OTP has also repatriated around EUR 774.4 million in dividends from its Russian subsidiary. Csányi said limited progress in bringing additional dividends out of Russia was one reason for the strategic review.

OTP agreed in July to acquire Luminor Holding from DNB and funds managed by Blackstone. The Baltic banking group operates across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. The deal would strengthen OTP’s position in the euro area while putting renewed focus on its continued presence in Russia. Estonian Finance Minister Jürgen Ligi has said the bank’s Russian operations are a moral shame, while Baltic regulators have also raised concerns.

OTP has already scaled back in Russia and laid eyes on something else

OTP Bank Group has continued operating in Russia since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, although it says it has substantially reduced its activities there. The bank suspended corporate lending after the outbreak of the war and withdrew intra-group financing from its Russian subsidiary. Its current Russian operations are largely focused on retail consumer lending and deposits.

OTP said it has reduced its Russian workforce by 25 per cent and its branch network by 40 per cent. At the same time, its Ukrainian business has expanded, with the bank reporting a 35 per cent increase in its loan portfolio in 2025.

Bloomberg documents raise questions

Bloomberg reported that documents it reviewed show that some OTP customers included companies controlled by Gazprom, while other customers provided services to organisations linked to Russian intelligence. One set of emails from April and May 2026 discussed a potential payment arrangement involving Gazprom Export, Gazprom-controlled Yugorosgaz and Gazprom subsidiary Rosingaz.

Under one proposed arrangement, money would have been transferred from a Yugorosgaz euro account at OTP Serbia to a Rosingaz account at Serbia’s state-owned Banka Poštanska Štedionica. The documents do not establish that the transaction was completed. OTP said it conducted an internal review following Bloomberg’s questions and found no evidence that any member of the OTP Group had breached applicable sanctions. The bank reiterated its commitment to complying with UN, EU, US and UK sanctions.

Leaving won’t be so easy

Selling the Russian subsidiary could prove complicated. OTP says Russian rules and international restrictions make finding an acceptable buyer difficult, while sellers leaving Russia can realise only a fraction of an asset’s market value. The bank has previously said that selling its Russian business is currently “practically impossible”.

OTP therefore faces a strategic choice between retaining a profitable but increasingly isolated operation and pursuing a deeper European focus through its planned Luminor acquisition. The outcome of the review, expected by the end of the year, could determine the future of OTP’s two-decade presence in Russia.

World.title: Green light for 280 new Budapest homes as huge development acquires permits
World.content:
Belgian property developer Atenor has secured a building permit for BakerStreet II, a new residential development in Budapest’s 11th district that will bring 280 apartments to the capital’s housing market.

Three buildings and 26,700 square metres of residential space

The project is a big change in direction for the site, which was originally intended for office development. Atenor has reassessed the concept in response to changing conditions in Budapest’s property market and the company’s growing focus on residential projects. Construction and pre-sales are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with completion scheduled for the second quarter of 2029.

BakerStreet II will comprise three buildings containing a total of 280 homes, with approximately 26,700 square metres of residential space. A landscaped inner courtyard will form a central feature of the development, incorporating substantial green areas as well as communal facilities designed for residents. The project is situated in an established and developing part of the 11th district, with access to the Danube and nearby university campuses.

Atenor Hungary managing director János Martin said BakerStreet II, together with the company’s Lake 11 development, would strengthen its residential offering in a well-connected and rapidly developing part of Budapest, quotes Portfolio. The shift towards residential development reflects a broader change in Atenor’s strategy in the Hungarian capital, where housing projects are becoming an increasingly important part of its assets.

The inner park of the planned project. Source: Atenor

BakerStreet II joins Lake 11

The new development will complement Lake 11, another major Atenor residential project in Budapest’s 11th district, near Lake Kána. Lake 11 is being developed in several phases and is ultimately planned to include nearly 900 apartments, alongside approximately 2,300 square metres of commercial space. The first phase, Lake 11 Home&Park, consists of 265 apartments and has already been completed.

BakerStreet II will add 280 homes to the capital’s future housing supply once completed in 2029. With the project now having received its building permit, the next major milestones are expected to be the launch of pre-sales and construction in early 2027. The development, alongside the continuing Lake 11 project, underlines the growing scale of Atenor’s residential activities in Budapest’s 11th district.

World.title: Former Orbán-era minister detained over alleged corruption: here’s what happens if he’s convicted
World.content:
Former National Development Minister Miklós Seszták has been detained at Hungary’s Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office after Parliament suspended his immunity over corruption allegations dating back to his time in government.

Seszták detained after going to prosecutor’s office

Miklós Seszták, a Christian Democrat MP and former Minister of National Development, was detained on Monday at the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office, his lawyer, Gábor Papp, told 24.hu.

Seszták did not attend Parliament for the vote on his immunity. Instead, he went to the prosecutor’s office, saying that he intended to give a statement. He maintains that he is innocent.

Earlier on Monday, Parliament voted 139–0, with no abstentions, to suspend Seszták’s parliamentary immunity. The decision allows criminal proceedings against him to move forward in connection with corruption cases outlined by prosecutors last week.

If convicted, Seszták could face up to 10 years in prison.

Prosecutors allege billions in illegal benefits

The Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office has alleged that there are well-founded grounds to suspect that Seszták accepted bribes worth hundreds of millions or even several billion forints from construction contractors while serving as Minister of National Development between 2014 and 2018.

According to prosecutors, Seszták and Norbert Szivek, who was CEO of the Hungarian National Asset Management Company at the time, obtained HUF 11 billion (approximately EUR 30 million) in unlawful benefits.

The prosecution has also referred to other incriminating testimony against Seszták. These are allegations, and Seszták has denied committing any crime.

After prosecutors requested the suspension of his immunity, he previously said that every element of the allegations was unfounded.

“I have not committed any crime, and I am not aware of any crime having been committed,”

he said at the time.

Living, working or doing business in Hungary?

Make things easier with professional support in English. Explore Daily News Hungary’s Services in English and find the help you need.

A political career spanning decades

Seszták, born in 1968, graduated in law from Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest in 1994 and began working as a lawyer two years later, Telex writes.

He entered local politics in Kisvárda in 1998 and became a member of the National Assembly for the Fidesz–KDNP alliance in 2010. He won the Kisvárda constituency again in 2014, 2018 and 2022.

He served as Minister of National Development from 2014 to 2018, overseeing a ministry with responsibility for a wide range of economic and state-owned assets.

Seszták remained a member of Parliament after leaving government and was among Hungary’s wealthiest MPs for years. He entered the current Parliament from the Fidesz–KDNP national list as a member of the KDNP parliamentary group.

However, he lost his Kisvárda constituency in the 2026 election, when Tisza candidate Viktória Dicső defeated him by six percentage points.

If you missed it: Breaking: Hungarian parliament suspends PM Magyar’s immunity over alleged phone theft

Previous controversies surrounding Seszták

These corruption allegations are not the first controversy to have surrounded Seszták. In 2013, before he became minister, Átlátszó reported that five companies had won a combined HUF 12.5 billion in funding in a tender for developing broadband optical networks. The companies had reportedly been established shortly beforehand and registered at the same address, while belonging to a group in which Seszták had served as a supervisory board member.

In 2014, Index reported that Seszták had been involved over several years in establishing hundreds of companies, many registered in the names of Russian and Ukrainian nationals at addresses in Kisvárda. According to the report, more than 700 companies were involved, many of which were later liquidated with outstanding debts.

Seszták has also remained one of the wealthier members of Parliament. His 2026 asset declaration lists two properties in Budapest and three in Kisvárda, as well as HUF 869 million in government securities, HUF 103 million in investment funds and HUF 32.7 million in shares. He declared HUF 66 million in bank deposits and HUF 20 million in cash.

The current corruption allegations concern events from Seszták’s period as minister between 2014 and 2018. The suspension of his immunity and his detention do not amount to a finding of guilt; any criminal liability will ultimately be determined through the judicial process.

World.title: Kosovo MPs Voice ‘Deep Concern’ Over Guerrilla Leaders’ Conviction
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Kosovo MPs in session on September 28, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

In a rare show of unanimity, Kosovo MPs on Monday adopted a statement expressing “deep concern” over this month’s Hague court conviction for war crimes of four former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA – Hashim Thaci, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi.

The statement supported by 99 MPs calls on Kosovo’s institutions to take action “to protect the truth and purity of the liberation war of the people of Kosovo”. Ethnic Serb MPs from the Belgrade-backed Srpska Lista party were not present for the vote.

The text calls for the drafting of a common state strategy that would coordinate actions “for the protection and affirmation of the full historical truth about the just war for freedom and liberation of Kosovo.

“[Parliament] considers the conclusion [of the verdict] on the existence of a common criminal intent unacceptable,”= the statement added.

Kosovo’s ex-President, Thaci, and his co-defendants, former parliament speakers Krasniqi and Veseli and former MP Selimi, were sentenced to 25, 25, 18 and 13 years in jail respectively on September 16.

All four were found guilty of responsibility for crimes carried out while they were senior officials of the KLA during the 1998-99 war with Serbian forces.

They were found not guilty of crimes against humanity, of persecution, imprisonment, other inhumane acts, torture, murder and enforced disappearances.

Thaci, Veseli, Krasniqi and Selimi all pleaded not guilty to all charges and will appeal the verdict.

Since the verdict was announced, hundreds of people have been protesting in the capital, Pristina, and in other cities in Kosovo and abroad. Many Kosovo Albanians deem the Hague verdict an attack on the KLA’s just war for liberation.

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was created specifically to try former members of the KLA, under pressure from Kosovo’s Western allies. The court is widely disliked in Kosovo, where it is seen as denigrating the KLA’s struggle.

Parallel with the statement, the opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo, PDK, is urging parliament to support amendments to the law on Specialist Chambers, approved in 2015, which would limit the scope of the chambers.

“Parliament has done its job, now it’s for the government to address the draft law [on the Specialist Chambers] responsibly. It should address it with urgency because there is no reason for delays. We saw with the Statement that there is a will. We expect the government to work on it today and send it to parliament tomorrow, or the day after,” Arian Tahiri, head of the PDK parliamentary group, said on Monday.

World.title: Serbia’s Vucic Pardons ‘Novi Sad 12’ as ‘Act of Mercy’ Before Resigning
World.content:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic on Sunday said he had pardoned 12 anti-government activists from the city of Novi Sad who are on trial for allegedly preparing “acts against the constitutional order”, in one of his final decisions as President as he announced his resignation before next month’s elections.

Vucic said he had pardoned a total of 49 people, including 23 who are connected to what he called “all these terrible events over the past year and a half” – a reference to mass student-led protests that have shaken his government – including the so-called ‘Novi Sad 12’.

“I made the decision to pardon 12 people from the Novi Sad group led by [activist] Mila Pajic, just as I decided to pardon 11 people who, on the other [pro-government] side, took part in incidents against protesters involved in the blockades,” Vucic said in a speech in Belgrade before submitting his resignation.

He described the decision as an “act of mercy because of their age, not because they are not guilty of something or did not do something. I did so because I know they would have been sentenced to several years in prison in any country, in any other country in the world. And I want to protect every young person because I believe there is hope that they will change and behave much more responsibly in the future,” Vucic said.

He said he had made the decision despite advice from the security services.

The 12 activists, linked to the opposition Free Citizens Movement, PSG, and the activist group Students Against Authoritarian Rule, STAV, were charged with preparing acts against Serbia’s constitutional order and security.

The charges arose from a recording of the meeting between the indictees ahead of a March 2025 rally that became the largest in Serbian history.

Six of them spent more than seven months in detention and house arrest before being released to defend themselves at liberty.

The other six were outside Serbia when the arrests took place and have remained abroad, with proceedings against them conducted in absentia.

One of the six activists in exile, Doroteja Antic, told BIRN that none of them wanted the case to end with a pardon from Vucic, who she claimed was again using the group “for his own political purposes, to score political points”.

“He did not do this out of kindness but solely because it is politically advantageous for him at this moment. And this is the final proof that the case was fabricated and politically constructed from the very beginning, and that there was never really a case at all,” Antic said.

She acknowledged that this should end the court proceedings being conducted against the 12 activists.

“We are now waiting for the final confirmation and official notices from the court that the proceedings have been discontinued, but that is expected to happen soon, at least according to our lawyers,” Antic explained.

However, she said that her plan is to remain outside Serbia while Vucic remains in power, to ensure she is safe.

“My plan is to stay here at least until the elections, in the great hope that after October 25 we will all meet again in a free Serbia, because this really feels like the final moment, the last gasp and cry of a government that people have long wanted to see the back of,” she said.

World.title: Finance Minister: Moldova Mustn’t Waste EU Funds Intended for Reforms
World.content:
Moldova is preparing draconian but necessary economic and financial reforms designed to align the country with EU standards, says Finance Minister Victoria Belous, and turn the post-Soviet republic into a European one.

However, turning EU financing into better public services is not simple, Belous told BIRN in an interview. Administrative delays are holding up investment, even as the government seeks to finance higher public-sector salaries and prepares tax changes for 2027, she explains.

“The problem for public investment projects is not lack of money but the capacity and efficiency of certain processes which, unfortunately, delay implementation,” Belous said.

This distinction runs through the government’s reform plans generally: spending commitments require dependable income, while investment requires institutions capable of putting projects into practice.

World.title: Hostile Reactions to Kosovo Wartime Leaders’ Verdict Miss Key Point: the Victims’ Ordeal
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

The first-instance verdict in the trial of Hashim Thaci, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers was received in Belgrade and Pristina in a predictable manner: as yet another event interpreted through national political narratives.

Belgrade believes the sentences were not severe enough, that the court protected the interests of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, and that it failed to sufficiently take into account the crimes committed against Serbs.

In Pristina, politicians deemed the verdict unjust, and thousands of people took to the streets to express support for the convicted former KLA leaders.

There is nothing new in such reactions. We have witnessed similar responses regarding the verdicts of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, ICTY.

World.title: Failings of Bosnia’s ‘Trojka’ Offer Unreformed SDA a Path Back
World.content:
For months, the leadership of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s main Bosniak opposition party, the Party of Democratic Action, SDA, has carefully nurtured a singular political narrative: their return to power is not just an ambition, but a mathematical certainty.

After being pushed into the opposition benches in 2022 by a diverse coalition of civic and multi-ethnic parties known as the ‘Trojka’ [The Trio], the SDA under Bakir Izetbegovic has used the campaign for next month’s elections to frame the current administration as a failed foreign-imposed experiment.

However, beneath the confident rhetoric and aggressive campaign videos, independent analysts say the SDA’s triumphant comeback might be more of an internal propaganda illusion than a reality reflected in public sentiment.

Instead of a structural resurgence, the political landscape reveals a deeper, more systemic stagnation where voters feel trapped between an uninspired opposition and a ruling coalition that has rapidly absorbed the very governing vices it once promised to dismantle.

World.title: Bosnia Court Blocks Republika Srpska From Funding Secessionist Lobbying
World.content:
Bosnian lawmaker Denis Zvizdic, who initiated teh legal challenge. Photo: EPA/FELIPE TRUEBA.

Bosnia’s Constitutional Court on Friday declared that budgetary funds used by Bosnia’s Serb-dominated Republika Srpska entity to pay foreign consulting firms to lobby for independence violate the state’s constitutional architecture.

The ruling targets a consulting agreement signed between the Republika Srpska Representative Office in Vienna and a Montreal-based firm, Dickens & Madson Canada Inc., which listed “the independence of Republika Srpska” as a core political objective.

The legal challenge was initiated in April by a state-level lawmaker, Denis Zvizdic, who argued that using taxpayers’ funds to lobby against Bosnia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity was unconstitutional.

A 2008 ruling allowed the entity to engage foreign firms for general economic promotion. However, the court has now established that funding campaigns explicitly promoting secession represents an assault on the constitutional order.

“The Constitutional Court hereby prohibits all payments from the budget of Republika Srpska regarding the consulting services contract concluded with Dickens & Madson Canada Inc.,” the court said. “Financing lobbying services for goals that run counter to the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina is strictly incompatible with the constitutional order.”

The applicant, Zvizdic, welcomed the announcement, saying the entity had weaponised massive public funds for anti-state campaigns.

“Public money cannot be used to finance lobbying aimed against the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, its territorial integrity, sovereignty and its institutions,” Zvizdic stated.

“This binding decision establishes a clear legal standard: citizens’ money must serve development and investment, not the undermining of the state,” he added.

Under Bosnia’s state-level laws, entities possess no constitutional right to unilateral secession. Furthermore, ignoring or violating a binding order of the Constitutional Court carries severe penalties.

The court said the full text of the judicial decision will be delivered to all parties and published on its official website within the month.

World.title: Week in Review: Spyware, AI and Arrests
World.content:
Montenegro’s parliament failed to debate a motion to dismiss Andrija Mandic of the right-wing New Serbian Democracy party as speaker because there was no quorum to hold the session. The motion came after Mandic sent a message of condolence to the son of the former Bosnian Serb military commander and genocide convict Ratko Mladic following his recent death.

This episode has renewed questions about how much Mandic’s politics have changed. The one-time opponent of Montenegro’s independence and NATO membership has become a speaker of parliament who now regularly speaks about Montenegro’s European future and works with European officials.

World.title: Croatia and USA to Strengthen Ties Across Multiple Sectors
World.content:
September the 29th, 2026 – Croatia and the USA are set to strengthen ties across multiple sectors, from tourism to investments, energy and tech.

The recent Economic Forum in New York, organised by the Croatian Chamber of Economy (HGK) and the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ), brought together around 70 American and 35 Croatian companies, including 15 from the tourism sector.

Domagoj Puljizovic reports for Poslovni that over 100 business people from both sides of the Atlantic took part, with the goal of strengthening economic cooperation between Croatia and the USA, connecting companies, opening new business partnerships and creating opportunities for investment and business expansion on the American market. Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković also attended the forum together with entrepreneurs from Croatia and the USA, discussing the further development of economic relations between the two countries. B2B meetings were also in focus, enabling direct company connections and the presentation of opportunities for future cooperation.

important croatian companies took part

President of the Croatian Chamber of Economy Luka Burilović emphasised that some of the most important Croatian companies from the energy, food industry and defence sectors participated in the economic delegation. “The strongest Croatian companies from energy, the food industry and defence are taking part in the economic delegation. Some of them are already present in the USA, including Orqa, Končar, Infobip, HS Produkt, Metamorfoza, Podravka and many others. Interest in cooperation is high, and the potential is even greater. This is confirmed by the impressive turnout, both in number and composition, of more than 100 businesspeople from the American side,” said Burilović.

new business bridges

He added that the partnership between Croatia and the USA is strengthening year by year, and that existing cooperation agreements provide an important framework for its further development. As one of the important steps in strengthening economic cooperation, he highlighted the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, which was signed almost four years ago but has not yet entered into force. Its application is expected to reduce business costs and administrative barriers and further encourage investments, especially in the IT sector.

Prime Minister Plenković emphasised that Croatia wants to further develop its partnership with the USA in areas of strategic importance for future economic development – from energy and technology to industry and innovation. “We see particular potential in energy, digital technologies and artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, the defence industry, research and development, and high-tech investments. The expanded LNG terminal on Krk will reach a capacity of 6.1 billion cubic metres per year, and more than two-thirds of the gas arriving at Krk comes from the USA,” said Plenković.

croatia’s blossoming ict sector

He also highlighted the importance of Croatia’s ICT sector, whose globally successful companies confirm the potential of domestic knowledge, talent and innovation. He stressed that Croatia should be viewed not only as a market of 4 million people, but also as a safe and stable base for access to the European Union market of 450 million consumers.

“We want to connect Croatian and American companies, capital, technology and knowledge even more strongly. We want to further develop tourism sustainably, with investments in higher-quality accommodation, infrastructure, services and stronger air connections with the USA. We are building new transatlantic value chains and opening space for an even stronger economic partnership between Croatia and the USA,” the Prime Minister said.

further tourism opportunities

Tourism was one of the important topics of the forum. Croatian service exports to the USA have amounted to almost one billion euros in recent years, and a significant part of the revenue is generated precisely in this area, along with IT and consulting services. HTZ Director Kristjan Staničić said that the American market shows great interest in Croatia’s tourism offer, especially the premium segment and high value-added products.

“The USA is Croatia’s most important long-haul market, with great potential. American guests are among our tourists with the highest average spending, they increasingly visit Croatia throughout the year, and interest in investing in Croatian tourism is also growing,” said Staničić. He added that discussions were also held on continuing cooperation to improve air connectivity between the USA and Croatia. He also highlighted the promotion of Croatia through a new promotional video featuring John Malkovich, which is being shown on Times Square in New York, one of the world’s most famous tourist locations.

World.title: Largest Thermal Baths in Croatia Open As Of Today
World.content:
September the 29th, 2026 – The largest thermal baths in Croatia have opened their doors today, putting Bjelovar and the massive Wellovar project in the spotlight.

Construction lasted 23 long months, and it is the most complex pool complex in Croatia due to its energy, heating, air-conditioning and cooling systems. Poslovni reports that the geothermal baths called Wellovar in Bjelovar will be officially opened today on the occasion of City Day. The thermal baths themselves will be available to the general public in about ten days, Mayor Dario Hrebak announced on Monday.

Today marks 270 years of the city of Bjelovar and the Wellovar project is the largest project in its history, and all of the necessary occupancy permits for the baths have been obtained. The complex has five indoor and five outdoor pools, including an Olympic-size one, four saunas, a gym, sports and recreational facilities, and a restaurant. The outdoor pools will open only next year in May because it’s currently too cold.

According to Terme Bjelovar director Zvonimir Žarec, there are currently 47 employees at the baths, and lifeguards will also be hired shortly. Žarec said that in the last seven to eight months he has spoken with more than a thousand candidates, and a large part of the employees have returned to Bjelovar from other places.

Three hours of swimming on a weekday will cost seven euros, and a full-day ticket 16 euros on weekdays or 21 euros at weekends and on public holidays. Pensioners, persons with disabilities, war veterans, students and secondary-school pupils will pay five euros for three hours of swimming in the morning hours. A full-day family ticket for two adults and two children will cost 44 euros on weekdays or 56 euros at weekends and on public holidays.

Around 600 guests are expected at the ceremonial opening and session, and the arrival of Prime Minister Andrej Plenković and Speaker of the Croatian Parliament Gordan Jandroković has also been announced.

World.title: First Croatian Green Hydrogen Plant Being Built at Rijeka Refinery
World.content:
September the 29th, 2026 – The very first Croatian green hydrogen plant is being built at the large Rijeka Refinery, and it’s one of INA’s key investments.

Croatia will soon get its first commercial plant for the production of green hydrogen. Morski reports that the INA industrial complex at the Rijeka Refinery is currently a major construction site, and the first molecules of this more environmentally friendly energy source are expected at the beginning of next year, according to HRT. This is otherwise one of INA’s key investments, worth more than 60 million euros, which significantly strengthens Croatia’s energy position on the European map.

1,500 tonnes of hydrogen per year

Designed in accordance with the best global practices and technologies already applied worldwide, the new hydrogen production plant will use electricity from its own power plant. “Similar plants have already been implemented around the world, and ours is being built to the highest standards,” emphasised Una Radulović Zekić, Director of Health, Safety and Environment at INA. The planned annual capacity is 1,500 tonnes of green hydrogen. It will primarily be used for the needs of the refinery itself, but depending on demand, it will also be available for placement on the commercial market.

This project is part of a broader modernisation cycle of the Rijeka plant, within which the construction of a facility for processing heavy residues was recently completed. This enables the processing of a significantly wider range of crude oil and completely eliminates the need to import semi-finished products, while overall diesel production will increase by up to 30 percent. Goran Pleše, Operational Director of Refining and Marketing at INA, emphasises that with the completed modernisation, both Rijeka and Croatia are gaining a much more favourable market position.

kostrena demands higher environmental standards

Despite these large investments, the local community points to long-standing open environmental problems. Residents of Kostrena have been struggling for decades with unpleasant odours and occasional sea pollution. “Kostrena has been burdened by all kinds of industry in the area for decades. We expect INA and others to move in the direction of relief and to respect the highest standards of environmental protection, safety and transparency,” said the mayor of the Municipality of Kostrena, Dražen Vranić.

a new system of protective barriers for a cleaner sea

Responding to environmental challenges, INA points out that the construction of an extensive system of protective barriers is also underway, which should prevent further leakage of hydrocarbons into the marine area. The project envisages the drilling of a total of 75 boreholes, of which 54 are new and 21 existing. The entire system is designed to pump pollutants at the lowest point and thus permanently prevent contact of hydrocarbons with the sea. Completion of the works and the first concrete results are expected in the spring.

World.title: Sahara Heatwave Heading for Europe – What Awaits Croatia?
World.content:
September the 29th, 2026 – Yet another heatwave is due to arrive in Europe from Africa, but what does it mean for temperatures in Croatia?

Currently, a very deep and slow-moving cyclone is located over the Atlantic, with its centre situated between Iceland and Great Britain. Its eastward progress is blocked by a field of high pressure over central and eastern Europe. Index reports that from the front side of the cyclone, together with upper-level flow from the southeast, a warm and dry air mass of Saharan origin is arriving over the European mainland, according to N1 Television meteorologist Bojan Lipovščak.

with another heatwave coming, what can croatia expect?

The field of elevated pressure over Croatia and the immediate region is supporting clear and stable weather. On the Adriatic coast and the islands, a weak to moderate anticyclonic bura is blowing. Due to the clear nights, morning and night-time temperatures inland are relatively low, so light frost is possible in places near the ground. After sunrise, air temperatures rise quickly, and the daily temperature range reaches up to 20 °C in some places, which requires appropriate layered clothing.

the forecast for the coming week

Today the weather will be sunny, with weak development of daytime cloudiness in the mountainous areas of the interior. In Slavonia, Baranja and Srijem, increased cloudiness from the northeast is expected during the afternoon and evening. The highest daily temperatures inland and on the Adriatic will be between 22 and 27 °C. On the Adriatic, a moderate tramontana and maestral will blow, while on the far south of Dalmatia a strong bura is expected in gusts. On Tuesday, after local morning fog, it will be sunny and one to two degrees warmer than on Monday. Morning temperatures inland will be around 8 °C, and on the Adriatic around 15 °C. The highest daily temperatures will range from 21 to 27 °C.

On the Adriatic coast, a weak to moderate maestral will blow, and in the Podvelebit coastal area and the south of Dalmatia up to a moderate bura.

the weather conditions until mid-october

Stable and warm weather continues throughout the week. A change in the weather that should bring precipitation and a drop in temperature is likely only around the 10th of October. The bura wind has pushed the warm surface layer of the sea towards the open sea, so sea temperatures have fallen and currently range between 22 and 24 °C.

World.title: Croatia Has Highest Number of Overnight Stays Relative to Number of Inhabitants
World.content:
September the 28th, 2026 – Croatia has the highest number of overnight stays relative to the number of inhabitants according to the latest Eurostat data.

Croatia has officially taken first place on the ranking of countries with the highest number of tourist overnight stays relative to the number of inhabitants. According to the latest Eurostat data, for every 1,000 inhabitants of Croatia, as many as 24,465 overnight stays in tourist accommodation are recorded annually. Index reports that this indicator does not refer to the total number of tourists, but compares the number of overnight stays with the number of inhabitants, so smaller countries that attract a large number of visitors during the year often end up at the top.

croatia steams ahead of malta and cyprus

According to data for 2025, Croatia is in first place ahead of Malta, which has 20,091 overnight stays per 1,000 inhabitants, and Cyprus with 18,533 overnight stays. Among the top ten are also Greece with 14,741 overnight stays, Austria with 14,619, Spain with 10,390, Italy with 9,084, Slovenia with 8,366, Montenegro with 8,339 and Portugal with 8,319 overnight stays per 1,000 inhabitants. Also on the list are the Netherlands with 8,102 and Ireland with 7,788 overnight stays per 1,000 inhabitants.

significant growth for croatia

Croatia reached the top of this ranking after strong tourism growth over the past decade. While Cyprus and Malta previously led according to this indicator, Croatia overtook them in 2016. Growing interest in Croatia was further boosted by the increasing popularity of Adriatic destinations, better connections with European markets, and the global recognition of certain locations. Among the factors that contributed to Croatia’s greater visibility is the popularity of the places where the series “Game of Thrones” was filmed.

By 2025, Croatia had reached 24,465 overnight stays per 1,000 inhabitants, which is about 1.22 times more than Malta, which is in second place.

small european countries attract plenty of attention

The ranking shows that the countries with the highest intensity of tourism are mostly smaller European states that receive a large number of visitors during the year relative to their population. For Croatia, this means that during the tourist season the number of people in individual coastal towns and places multiplies compared to the number of permanent residents.

World.title: Croatia Remains in a Favourable Position With Gas Reserves
World.content:
September the 28th, 2026 – Croatia continues to be in a very favourable position when it comes to gas reserves as autumn and then winter approach.

The Croatian Government has ordered the mandatory acceleration of gas stock filling so that the Okoli underground storage facility reaches the target level of at least 85 percent of capacity by October. Zrinka Gabelica Toplek reports for Poslovni that Croatia ended the summer with an enviable 73 percent gas storage fill level, placing it well above the EU average. While the rest of Europe is intensively preparing for the upcoming heating season, the situation across the continent varies considerably from country to country.

Nevertheless, joint European efforts are yielding results, as the EU average gas storage fill level stands at a solid 65 percent. At the very top of the ranking are Poland and Portugal, which already reached an excellent 93 percent of their capacity by the end of August. Neighbouring Italy also stands out with a high stock level of 83 percent. Croatia shares a high fourth place with Spain, as both countries have secured 73 percent of their stocks. Immediately behind them is France with 71 percent, while neighbouring Hungary records 69 percent and Austria 67 percent fill levels.

On the other hand, several key European economies are still lagging behind the average: Germany recorded only 53 percent storage fill at the end of summer, while Sweden and Slovakia secured exactly half of their capacity – just 50 percent. At the very bottom of the listed countries are the Netherlands with 47 percent and Latvia with 45 percent gas stocks.

This latest data suggest that Croatia is in a favourable position ahead of autumn and winter, but the overall picture at Union level shows that individual countries will have to accelerate the filling of gas storage in the coming weeks in order to achieve full energy security before the first serious cold spells. Although the current 73 percent fill level provides energy stability, the Croatian Government has ordered the mandatory acceleration of gas stock filling so that the Okoli underground storage facility reaches the target level of at least 85 percent of capacity by October, ahead of the official start of the heating season.

World.title: Croatian Agriculture Suffers Tremendously Due to Drought
World.content:
September the 28th, 2026 – Croatian agriculture as a sector has suffered tremendously as a result of long periods of drought this year, with arable land being the most vulnerable of all.

This year’s extreme and long periods of drought has significantly affected the arable production of Podravka Agri, and its final impact on revenues will only be known after all harvesting work is completed. The company told Hina that such a drought in eastern Croatia has not been recorded in the last 20 years. “Since the harvesting of individual crops is still under way, and the lifting of sugar beet has yet to begin, the impact of the drought on total arable revenues will be known only after all work is finished,” they said.

Ana Blaskovic reports for Poslovni that the prolonged lack of rainfall and extremely high temperatures particularly affected spring crops, including maize, soybeans and sugar beet, while sunflower performed somewhat better. An additional problem was the lack of irrigation possibilities due to historically low water levels of the Danube and Drava rivers during the summer months. Unlike the spring crops, winter wheat and barley did not suffer significantly because they finish their vegetation earlier, and their harvest was completed in the first half of July.

Climate extremes are becoming an increasingly important factor in planning agricultural production. At Podravka Agri, headed by Davor Doko, they note that in recent years they have been adapting production technologies and selecting more resistant hybrids and varieties in order to mitigate the consequences of climate change, preserve soil fertility and ensure the continuity of domestic food production.

On the other hand, the long period of dry weather this year also brought one positive consequence: it enabled the high-quality collection and storage of around 100,000 bales of straw, a quantity that will meet the needs of all 19 of Podravka Agri’s cattle farms.

World.title: Strikes Looming: Collapse Awaits Zagreb Today
World.content:
September the 28th, 2026 – Strikes will likely see the City of Zagreb totally collapse today, as ZET, Zagreb Holding and unions are set to down tools.

The management boards of Zagreb Holding and Zagreb Electric Tram (ZET) announced recently that a meeting with the unions failed to produce an agreement that would avert the strike today. According to their statement, the meeting was convened in another attempt to bring the positions of the employers and the unions closer and to prevent the strike.

“Despite acting in good faith, the representatives of the representative unions presented expanded demands to the managements of both companies as a condition for avoiding the strike, compared with those put forward during the mediation procedures,” the managements of Holding and ZET claim. Index reports that as an example, they cite the demand by the unions in Zagreb Holding for an increase in the base salary.

According to the managements, during mediation the unions sought a 12 percent increase in the base, while at today’s meeting they demanded 13 percent. “The managements of Zagreb Holding and ZET could not accept such an offer from the representative unions, which was presented as a condition for the strike not to take place,” they stated.

what do the unions say?

That no agreement was reached and that the strike will go ahead today was confirmed formally by Mumin Hodžić, president of the Union of Communal Workers and Drivers of Čistoća. He said the unions had “reduced” the percentage of the base salary increase to 13 percent, as well as the demands related to night-work and second-shift allowances. “We’ve given up on many things and we don’t intend to give up on anything else, especially since the other side has no other proposal except the one it already put forward,” he said.

Asked whether talks would continue tomorrow, he replied that they would not. “We came on Saturday at noon, we responded to the meeting, we put forward our offer with the aim of preventing the strike, reaching an agreement and avoiding the collapse that will happen today. However, the other side, which has constantly accused the unions of irresponsibility and this and that, came to the meeting only to hear what we would offer, while they themselves made no offer whatsoever,” he said.

“we were surprised by the offer from union reps”

Ivan Novaković, president of the Management Board of Zagreb Holding, told reporters that they were “totally surprised by the offer from the union representatives” because, he said, “they demanded more than their final offer at the end of mediation, so the meeting ended unsuccessfully.” Marko Bogdanović, president of the Management Board of ZET, said he expects arbitration at the beginning of next week to “provide an answer to the question of which essential services must continue during the strike.” The unions of ZET and Zagreb Holding had earlier sought a 19 percent increase in workers’ material rights, i.e. salaries, and the conclusion of collective agreements for a longer period. The managements had offered a 4.5 percent increase in the base salary.

the strike is due to begin today at 15:30, and the city will be left practically with zero public transport

Unless a new agreement is reached in the meantime, the strike by workers of ZET and Zagreb Holding has begun. The unions had previously announced that Zagreb could in that case be left practically without public transport. Dražen Jović, president of the Union of Transport and Communal Services of Croatia, said there is a high probability that not a single ZET vehicle will run after that point today.

The unions also described the situation by saying that if the strike goes ahead on the announced scale, people “will not see a single one of our vehicles.” Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević also warned that it is very likely that not a single tram will leave the depot and that public transport could come to a near-complete standstill during the day. He called on citizens who do not have to travel to stay at home, and on those who must go to work to leave earlier and expect significantly heavier traffic. He urged employers, where possible, to allow work from home and more flexible working hours. Tomašević also said that the City of Zagreb does not intend to pay workers for the days they spend on strike.

waste collection will also grind to a halt

The strike later today wouldn’t affect only ZET. Workers of Zagreb Holding perform a range of communal services, including waste collection, road maintenance and upkeep of green areas. The unions have announced that essential services will still be carried out. These include waste collection from hospitals, kindergartens, health centres and homes for the elderly, as well as burials. Regular household waste collection could, however, be entirely suspended or at the very least significantly reduced.

It has still not been fully resolved how many workers will have to continue to perform their essential duties during the strike. The managements of ZET and Holding proposed that a portion of employees continue working during the strike, but the unions rejected that proposal, which is why the matter has gone to arbitration.

World.title: 3 drones target Iranian opposition camp in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the Azadi camp, a facility affiliated with the opposition Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (PDKI) in the Koya district southeast of Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Monday.

According to the Kurdistan Regional Government’s (KRG) security agency, Asayish, the attacks took place in two waves between 1:40 and 2:10 a.m. local time.

The attack damaged the facility but resulted in no casualties.

Local Kurdish media, citing anonymous PDKI sources, claimed that the drones used in the attack were Iranian-made “Hadid” versions.

According to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-affiliated media agencies, the attacks targeted separatist organizations in the region.

Officials in Iraqi Kurdistan warned that the camp, which has housed displaced Iranian Kurds and the families of the party’s Peshmerga forces for over 25 years, has come under fire several times amid rising regional tensions.

The attack is the latest in a series of drone and missile strikes against Iranian Kurdish dissident sites in Iraq’s Kurdistan region.

World.title: Iraq officially declared as host of 2028 Arabian Gulf Cup
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has been officially announced as the host country for the 2028 Arabian Gulf Cup, which will be held in either Basra or Baghdad.

The Executive Office of the Arabian Gulf Cup Football Federation (AGCFF) ratified the decision during a meeting in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where Iraq made the only formal bid to host the event.

The tournament will take place from December 9 to December 22, 2028.

The 27th Arabian Gulf Cup is currently underway in Jeddah, running from September 23 to October 6, 2026.

While Basra is anticipated to be the primary location following the successful conclusion of the 2023 edition, Baghdad is still in contention.

The Iraqi Football Association (IFA) has set a deadline to formally confirm the host city and will be expected to meet all organizational criteria in accordance with authorized standards.

The decision marks the third time Iraq hosts the tournament, with the fifth edition in Baghdad in 1979 and the 25th edition in Basra in 2023.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to Jordan completely halt
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil exports to Jordan have completely stopped since the end of December 2025, despite ongoing negotiations this year aimed at resuming crude supplies to Amman.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that the halt in exports is linked to commercial matters and other factors involving Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) and the Jordanian side.

Al-Rikabi’s remarks come amid ongoing disputes regarding the terms of a new agreement. Informed sources had previously revealed Baghdad’s insistence on reducing tanker transport fees, while months of negotiations failed to result in a resumption of supplies.

Jordan used to receive approximately 10,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude—representing about seven percent of its oil needs—before shipments ceased at the end of 2025.

In January, Amman has not imported oil from Iraq, compared to approximately 309,712 barrels the previous month.

Iraq’s oil supplies to Jordan stood at around 299,824 barrels in November 2025, reflecting a steady flow of approximately 300,000 barrels per month during the period before the suspension takes place.

The previous annual contract expired on June 26, 2025, prior to a three-month extension running from October through December. The extension was intended to ensure the completion of the delivery of specified volumes that had been impacted by logistical challenges.

World.title: US troops completely withdraw from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi government official announced on Sunday that the withdrawal of the US troops from Iraq has been completed.

The official stated that both combat and logistical support personnel have departed the country, although there has been no formal confirmation from the US side, Sky News Arabia reported.

In 2024, Iraq and the United States agreed on a timeline to end the US military presence in the country. According to the US Department of Defense, approximately 2,500 US troops had been stationed in Iraq in the past few years.

Prior to the withdrawal, US forces were deployed across Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq, a base near Baghdad International Airport, and locations within the Green Zone in the capital, Baghdad.

US forces returned to Iraq in 2014 in response to a request by the Iraqi government—as part of the international coalition to combat ISIS—three years after their withdrawal following the 2003 US invasion.

While the terrorist group’s defeat in Iraq was announced in 2017, its cells remain in remote areas.

The withdrawal comes as Iraq faces security consequences linked to the conflict involving Iran, amid recent attacks targeting US facilities and forces.

World.title: India buys two million barrels of Iraqi oil at $28 discount per barrel
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Indian Oil Corp. (IOC), India’s largest state-owned refiner, has acquired 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil at a discount of almost $28 per barrel compared to the October Dubai benchmark.

The acquisition includes Basrah medium and heavy crude oil grades. IOC contracted to receive the cargo from the international trading business Mercuria on a free-on-board (FOB) basis, according to Reuters.

The crude is expected to be loaded and lifted between October 21 and October 31, 2026.

The enormous $28 reduction is due to significant regional logistics challenges. Shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which are associated with wider geopolitical tensions, have led to substantial increases in marine freight prices, insurance costs, and transit risks for buyers.

To address these export restrictions and ensure that its oil remains attractive to major global consumers like India, significant price discounts have been introduced. These discounts aim to offset the heightened risks that refiners encounter when arranging their own transportation.

This acquisition comes after IOC purchased one million barrels of October-loading Iraqi crude straight from Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) at a discount ranging between $23 and $28 per barrel only a few days ago.

World.title: Iraq recovers 80 smuggled artifacts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice successfully repatriated 80 smuggled historical artifacts and rare artworks on Monday, September 28, 2026, marking another breakthrough in federal legal campaigns to recover looted antiquities from abroad.

According to an official statement issued by the ministry, the restitution was finalized through intensive international legal proceedings managed by the Directorate of External Litigation, executed in direct operational coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy of the Republic of Iraq in Washington, D.C.

The ministry stated that the legal recovery operations, directed and monitored by Minister of Justice Dr. Khaled Shwani, form an integral part of Baghdad’s overarching policy to safeguard Iraq’s cultural heritage and reclaim sovereign historical assets dispersed through illicit trading networks.

Through its dedicated Department for the Recovery of Antiquities and Assets, the Directorate of External Litigation manages active cross-border claims, targeting antiquities illegally excavated from unmonitored archaeological digs as well as stolen cataloged pieces traded internationally in violation of Iraqi heritage statutes and UNESCO conventions.

Federal judicial authorities emphasized that these coordinated actions reflect the justice ministry’s structured legal mandate to track, document, and pursue stolen national assets worldwide.

By leveraging bilateral judicial agreements and working through diplomatic missions across North America and Europe, the Iraqi government aims to ensure the comprehensive preservation of Mesopotamia’s civilizational legacy and institutionalize robust legal frameworks against the illicit trafficking of cultural antiquities.

World.title: Gulf Cup 27: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar clinch semifinals as Iraq eyes decisive clash
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Matchday Two of the group stage at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup in Jeddah concluded with three national teams securing early qualification for the semifinals, leaving the remaining knockout berth in Group A contested ahead of the final group round.

Host nation Saudi Arabia confirmed its place in the final four alongside Group B qualifiers the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, while regional football powerhouses Kuwait, Bahrain, and Yemen suffered early mathematical elimination from tournament contention.

In Group A, tournament hosts Saudi Arabia solidified their standing at the summit of the table with a maximum of 6 points and a positive four goal difference following back-to-back victories. Iraq occupies second place with 4 points and a plus-one goal differential, having recorded one win and one draw across their opening fixtures.

Oman sits third with 1 point and a negative three goal differential, while Kuwait trails at the bottom of the group with zero points and a negative two goal difference. The distribution leaves Iraq positioned for a decisive final-round Gulf derby against Saudi Arabia, coinciding with the simultaneous encounter between Oman and Kuwait to determine the group’s second qualifying spot.

Group B witnessed a decisive resolution as both the United Arab Emirates and Qatar secured semifinal qualification with a match to spare, each accumulating 6 points from two consecutive victories. The UAE maintains the top position by virtue of an advantageous goal difference of plus-seven compared to Qatar’s plus-three.

Yemen and Bahrain sit eliminated at the foot of the table without points, both carrying identical negative five goal differentials. The final group fixtures will settle group positioning between the two leading sides as the tournament bracket prepares for the knockout stage.

World.title: Iraq officially licenses Starlink satellite internet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC) confirmed on Sunday, September 27, 2026, that satellite internet provider Starlink has secured an official operational license, formally legalizing its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite broadband services across Iraqi territory.

Speaking to the official state news agency, CMC Chief Executive Officer Baligh Abu Kalal dismissed claims that Iraqi telecommunications traffic and user data are hosted or routed through Qatar, stating that federal security authorities maintain complete sovereign oversight over all network operations and registered hardware within the country.

The licensing milestone follows public contention between federal regulatory bodies and the Ministry of Communications. In mid-August 2026, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad argued that the ground gateway servicing Iraq was located in Qatar, raising sovereignty concerns regarding regional content filtering, pornography blocks, and executive internet throttling during national examinations and public demonstrations.

Sanad had framed terrestrial Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) expansion as Iraq’s premier digital priority against foreign satellite conglomerates. Responding to these concerns, Abu Kalal clarified that Starlink’s regulatory framework incorporates a rigorous security annex, granting Iraqi intelligence and regulatory apparatuses real-time visibility into all active terminals, user registries, and equipment distributed nationally.

Abu Kalal explained that while initial deployment encountered minor delays due to multi-agency security vetting, the first batch of customer subscription terminals has been released, with sequential hardware shipments proceeding smoothly to fulfill pending consumer orders via the company’s official portal.

Although Starlink originally scheduled the construction of domestic terrestrial ground stations within two years, surging local demand has prompted expedited bilateral negotiations to install local ground gateways across Iraq ahead of schedule.

The CMC executive stressed that satellite internet governance relies fundamentally on sovereign licensing frameworks, statutory compliance, and contractual obligations, ensuring that national security protocols remain fully enforced regardless of atmospheric broadcast mechanics.

Minors on social media: SC asks Centre to enforce 18-year age threshold by law

NEW DELHI: Agreeing with Supreme Court, Centre on Monday said it would soon insert a provision in the Information and Technology Intermediary Rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing children under 18 years of age to open social media accounts, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.Agreeing with the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana as well as petitioner NGO 'Just Rights for Children Alliance' counsel H S Phoolka, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the agreements entered into by intermediaries and minors were void contracts and these must be prevented.Membership of educational websites can be taken through consent of parents," solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, adding that Centre would step in to make it a statutory obligation for intermediaries not to allow minors to have social media accounts.Justice Bagchi said, "They have registered under the laws of US and imported into Indian digital space the restrictions which are applicable in US (on minors' opening accounts on social media platforms), which is impermissible under Indian law."When Mehta said "we will have to control intermediaries", the bench responded, "Our request to you - will Centre pass some directions under Intermediary Rules that they should fashion their software or platform in conformity with Indian laws?"The SG said, "They will have to conform to Indian laws and there is no doubt about it.Something can be done, something should be done and something will be done." Justice Bagchi said, "They must restrict, at least in registering membership, to a minimum threshold of 18 years." The SG agreed and said it must now be inserted in some law or rules to make intermediaries compliant with Indian laws.Senior advocate Phoolka said govt had certain guidelines on this issue, which needed enforcement. The SG said it must now be enforced through a statute. CJI Kant said it must be through a statutory mechanism as the SG said and asked govt to consider it and get back with a response.The NGO complained that "absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposes children to foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content."

World.title: FBI puts gangster Goldy Brar on Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has officially placed notorious gangster Satinderjeet Singh aka Goldy Brar, on its famed Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.

The announcement, made early Tuesday, by the FBIâs Los Angeles Field Office, marks a major escalation in international law enforcement efforts targeting transnational crime syndicates operating across North America and Asia.

Brar, who becomes the 543rd fugitive added to the historic list, faces multiple federal indictments in the United States, including Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) conspiracy, extortion, and narcotics trafficking.

According to federal prosecutors, the fugitive serves as the primary North American operational leader for the Lawrence Bishnoi Organized Crime Group. Operating from a prison cell in India via contraband communications, Bishnoi allegedly delegated international operations to trusted lieutenants like Brar.

The syndicate has been linked to a trail of violence across North America, including targeted assassinations, kidnappings, armed extortions, and large-scale drug smugglingâincluding the theft of over 500 kilograms of cocaine from rival cartels in the Los Angeles region.





Among the most high-profile offenses detailed in federal court documents is the June 2023 assassination of prominent political and religious figure "H.S.N." outside a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia.

Bishnoi and Brar are charged with ordering the targeted killing. Canadian authorities subsequently designated the Bishnoi syndicate as a terrorist entity in September 2025, highlighting its routine use of public violence and social media threat campaigns to extort individuals within Indian diaspora communities worldwide.

World.title: Government deploys AI tool to scrutinise rural road project DPRs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a bid to cut down delays and improve quality, the government has deployed an AI-based detailed project report (DPR) scrutiny tool that aims at strengthening and streamlining the technical appraisal of rural road projects under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana.

Rolled out by rural development ministryâs National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency, last week, the tool, Parakh, has been implemented on a pilot basis in all states and UTs to assess its applicability and effectiveness. DPR preparation is a critical stage in rural road development, involving assessment of alignment, geometry, pavement design, traffic, soil and subgrade conditions, drainage, cross-drainage structures, quantities and cost estimates.

With thousands of DPRs requiring multi-level technical scrutiny, the govt is hoping that this AI-enabled tool will substantially reduce repetitive scrutiny time, identify deficiencies at an early stage and facilitate faster processing of DPRs, thereby accelerating sanction, execution and timely completion of PMGSY works.

As of now the same parameters are often checked repeatedly at different scrutiny levels, resulting in duplication of effort and longer processing time.





Consequently, sanction of works gets delayed, affecting subsequent execution and completion.

Rural development secretary Rohit Kansal said, âTransparent and consistent technical scrutiny is essential for better planning and timely implementation of PMGSY projects. Through Parakh, AI is being used to make the scrutiny of DPRs simpler, more systematic and more evidence-based.â

World.title: UNFPA report: Migrant workers cite livelihood insecurity, low wages, poverty and debt as reasons for moving out for better life
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nearly 72% of migrant workers surveyed in three south Indian states felt that moving for work has improved their standard of living and more than half (around 57%) intended to continue working in their destination state, as per a new report.

At the same time, it turns out that over 86% of workers have no signed employment contracts and many face difficulties ranging from accessing welfare and essential services to experiencing language, communication and social barriers.

Clearly migration decisions are shaped strongly by livelihood insecurity and limited employment opportunities. Migrants cited low wages at origin, lack of jobs, better opportunities, irregular employment, poverty and debt among the principal reasons for moving.

These findings are part of the South India Interstate Migration Survey (SIIMS) 2026, that offers first-of-its-kind data on the changing nature of migration within India and on how migrant workers from other states (primarily from northern and eastern) live and work in Karnataka, Keralam and Tamil Nadu.

The study surveyed 1,824 migrant workers and covered sectors including agriculture, fishing and marine work, and daily labour in all three states.





It also covered hospitality in Keralam, textile and garment work in Tamil Nadu, and scrap collection in Karnataka.

Over 92% of the migrants came from West Bengal (26.2%), Bihar (21.8%), Assam (17.1%), Odisha (12%), UP (9.6%) and Jharkhand (5.6%).

Conducted by the International Institute of Migration and Development (IIMAD), the study was supported by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

It comes through that over 77% of the surveyed workers were recruited through non-contractor channels, nearly 58% are paid in cash with Rs 17640 the average monthly wage and the average working day being 9.87 hours. The report also brings into focus the gender disparity as it came through that women workers earned about Rs 3,313 less per month than men.

The data shows that just a little over 19% of migrant workers can easily use their welfare benefits when they move between states; 35% can do so partly and around 45% can barely do so.

It also comes through that over 73% face problems accessing welfare and 69% face problems accessing healthcare.

The survey found that while 88.2% of migrant workers are included in formal financial services, exclusion was higher in Karnataka (26.8%) and among scrap collection workers (31.3%).

World.title: Cachar police arrest man over 'communally provocative’ social media posts
World.content:
A 29-year-old man was detained on Monday in the Cachar region of Assam for allegedly making "communally provocative" statements on social media, according to authorities.

According to the police, Kalparnab Gupta, who claims to be an IIT-Bombay research scholar and the head convenor of the Barak Union for Civil Liberties on Facebook, was taken into custody after a Bajrang Dal activist filed a complaint at the Silchar police station.

The man was accused in the complaint of posting "defamatory, hateful and communally provocative content" on Facebook that was directed against the Bajrang Dal, RSS, and Hinduism.

Additionally, Gupta was charged with trying to connect members of the Bajrang Dal to extortion schemes and a recent local gang rape assault.

World.title: Indian imports of Russian crude oil to decline further amid lower exports, Chinese competition
World.content:
Tourists watch marine life, with the MT Desert Kite oil tanker carrying Russian oil in the background (Photo: Reuters).

NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to decline further in October and November, owing to lower exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the country to buy costlier alternatives for the rest of the year.People familiar with procurement plans told Reuters that some Indian refiners would not receive adequate Russian supplies in October and November."Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners," a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said.According to analytics firm Kpler, Russian oil arrivals in India are set to drop to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest level since April.Trade data showed that arrivals had already fallen 16.5 per cent to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, although Russia remained India's main supplier, ahead of the UAE and Venezuela.Overall availability of Russian exports has reportedly shrunk, particularly from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have roughly halved as repeated drone attacks have suspended loadings.India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts.In recent months, however, China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as Middle Eastern supplies tightened because of the Iran war.Traders told Reuters that refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia's Urals grade, while also buying Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes.Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows to China.Seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) offers a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China, whereas shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis."It's not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination," another trader told Reuters, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.

World.title: 'First phase of Char Dham Yatra highly successful': Uttarakhand CM Dhami
World.content:
Uttarakhand Chief Minister

on Monday said the first phase of the Char Dham Yatra has been highly successful, while a large number of pilgrims continue to arrive during the second phase.

Dehradun (Uttarakhand) [India], September 28 (ANI): Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said the first phase of the Char Dham Yatra has been highly successful, while a large number of pilgrims continue to arrive during the second phase.

He said all necessary arrangements have been put in place to ensure a safe, smooth and well-organised pilgrimage, with the Disaster Management Department kept on alert across all districts associated with the yatra.

According to the Chief Minister's Office (CMO), senior officials at the state and district levels are continuously reviewing the arrangements and monitoring the situation. The Char Dham Yatra has been setting new records this year, with the state government maintaining close monitoring and making arrangements under the guidance of Chief Minister Dhami.

According to the state government, Badrinath and Gangotri Dham have recorded their highest-ever footfall, with 18.10 lakh pilgrims visiting Badrinath and a record 8.41 lakh devotees visiting Gangotri so far.





The number of pilgrims visiting Yamunotri has crossed 7.5 lakh, while 15.57 lakh pilgrims have visited Kedarnath. Overall, 53,23,401 pilgrims have visited the four Char Dham shrines so far this pilgrimage season, compared to around 46 lakh during the corresponding period last year, as per CMO.

World.title: Indo-French sat mission 'Trishna'  to map Earth's water sources on fast-track: Space minister Jitendra Singh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and France are preparing to launch 'Trishna' from Sriharikota in 2027 to monitor energy and water budgets of the Earth. The earth observation satellite 'Trishna' (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment), a collaborative endeavour between Isro and French space agency CNES, is engineered to deliver high spatial and high temporal resolution monitoring of Earth's surface temperature, emissivity, biophysical and radiation variables for surface energy budgeting at regional to global scale.

While meeting a big French delegation related to cooperation in the space and science sector, space and science minister Jitendra Singh said the realisation of the âjoint satellite, TRISHNA, is progressing well, and also appreciated CNES support to India's Gaganyaan programme, including supply of consumables and training of flight surgeonsâ. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.

The 'Trishna' mission will also help in a comprehensive assessment of urban heat islands, detection of thermal anomalies linked to volcanic activity and geothermal resources, and precise monitoring of snow-melt runoff and glacier dynamics. The mission will also provide valuable data on aerosol optical depth, atmospheric water vapor, and cloud cover.

A high-level French delegation led by Philippe Baptiste, French minister for higher education, research and space, met Singh in Delhi on Monday and they talked about the Space Summit, India-France Year of Innovation 2026 and priorities in scientific and technological cooperation, including space, CEFIPRA and blue economy.





Singh said India-France space cooperation has evolved from the early sounding rocket experiments of the 1960s into a broad and expanding partnership encompassing joint satellite missions, launch vehicle technologies, human spaceflight and emerging space applications. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.

He said the next phase of India-France cooperation can bring together government institutions, industries and start-ups on both sides to create a larger ecosystem and wider resource pool.

Philippe Baptiste described 'Trishna' as a strong example of what India and France can achieve together, and welcomed greater cooperation in human spaceflight, astronaut health, microgravity research and parabolic flights.

World.title: U.S. prosecutors reopen Cornell gang rape case after outcry
World.content:
U.S. prosecutors reopened an investigation on Monday (September 28, 2026) into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University following claims the elite college failed to properly punish the men involved.

The alleged victim said in a civil lawsuit this month she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped in 2024 by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students.

Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students involved, several of whom were later expelled.

The newly-released details of the alleged incident have fuelled allegations that the university was too lenient and reignited a debate over sexual assault on U.S. campuses.

Matthew Van Houten, district attorney for Tompkins County in New York, said that he plans to file criminal charges against the seven men.

He said his office chose in 2024 not to prosecute because the victim's testimony did not establish a lack of consent, but had now decided to do so in light of her latest allegations.

"I recognise the reality that it can take years of therapy and healing for victims of sexual assaults to fully process and understand what happened to them," Mr. Van Houten said in a statement.

"Seeking justice sometimes requires us to reconsider or reopen cases when we are provided with additional evidence."

Kyle Kimball, vice president of university relations at Cornell, said the Ivy League school supports the decision to reinvestigate the case.

He also rejected a claim, made in the civil lawsuit, that the suspects were offered the opportunity to write essays to mitigate their conduct.

"Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false," Mr. Kimball said.

The 101-page civil lawsuit filed in New York gives graphic details on the alleged assault of the woman, whose identity is being protected.

Notably, it provides a screenshot of a Snapchat group message advertising "free pussy" during the incident, apparently an invitation for other fraternity members to take part.

The suit seeks financial damages from Cornell and the seven suspects, adding that the woman has suffered "severe emotional and psychological distress."

British actor Florence Pugh has voiced her anger about the case, saying she felt "uneasy and sick and anxious" after hearing about it.

"Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world," she wrote on Instagram.

"You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won't be harmed in return," Ms. Pugh said.
